Sports.title: Uefa preparing to bring criminal claims against Gianni Infantino over World Cup sale
Sports.content:
Uefa is preparing to make a criminal complaint against Gianni Infantino for alleged “criminal mismanagement” in connection with his failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan and has applied for the release of documents related to its conception.

In an explosive escalation of the war engulfing football’s governing bodies, Uefa has made separate applications in the United States for information, including from Fifa and the investment firm Thrive Capital.

The request explains Uefa and other interested parties are “preparing to bring criminal claims in Switzerland against Infantino and possible other Fifa officials and advisors for criminal mismanagement under Article 158 of the Swiss Criminal Code”.

Quick Guide How do I 

Thrive Capital, led by Joshua Kushner, was to be the lead investor in Infantino’s plan. Uefa has used a “section 1782” order in seeking release of the relevant documents. Such a request lets an interested party in a foreign legal proceeding ask for discovery of information from an entity based in the US.

The court documents pay particular attention to the “absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20bn” implied by Infantino’s scheme to sell a 20% chunk of Fifa tournaments for $4.2bn. The figure is claimed to be “neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer”.

Uefa claims “a valuation exceeding $30bn is readily supportable” through assessment of Fifa’s financial performance and market conditions. Additionally, comparisons are drawn with the deal Infantino pursued in 2018 with a consortium led by the Japanese firm SoftBank. The submission points out that the proposal, which was dropped, would have committed about $25bn for a 12-year interest in the Nations League and an expanded Club World Cup.

Infantino is accused of a “stunning dereliction of duty” in sidelining the Fifa Council when tabling the plan. In a surgical walk-through of what is known about FFE’s conception and its withdrawal, the documents also highlight the expedited timeline member associations were given to back the scheme and the $40m “inducement” they were offered to do so.

This month Uefa’s lawyers had told Infantino and Fifa to “take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control”. They had named 14 executives who were required to “specifically preserve all such materials in their possession, custody, or control”.

Uefa on Thursday filed a request for discovery in US District Court for the Eastern District of New York, which if granted would enable them to subpoena Kushner and Thrive for documents relating to Fifa’s FFE proposal, and allow Uefa attorneys to depose Kushner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to The Recap The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In a 56-page filing that contains a section headlined “the enduring history of corruption among Fifa officials”, Uefa’s attorneys describe FFE as “a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from Fifa’s most valuable assets to the detriment of Fifa, its members, and other parties within the football family”.

Uefa clarifies that “neither Thrive nor Kushner is an anticipated defendant in the contemplated Swiss criminal proceeding”.

Fifa and Thrive Capital have been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Liverpool agree £120m deal for Bradley Barcola after breakthrough talks with PSG
Sports.content:
Liverpool are closing in on a £120m deal for Bradley Barcola after a breakthrough in talks with Paris Saint-Germain and will attempt to “improve other areas” according to the head coach, Andoni Iraola.

Barcola has been Liverpool’s main transfer target all summer only for PSG’s £145m valuation to prove a significant hurdle. However, further negotiations on Wednesday night ended in an outline agreement being reached over a compromise fee. Liverpool have agreed to pay a guaranteed sum of just over £100m for the France international, with add-ons based on individual and team success, taking the overall package to about £120m.

The full structure of the deal has not been finalised, but Wednesday night’s breakthrough, coupled with PSG’s willingness to lower their asking price for the 23-year-old, should allow Barcola to complete his move before Tuesday’s transfer deadline. Liverpool were informed last month the player was keen to join them, having fallen down the pecking order at PSG.

Barcola has two years remaining on his PSG contract, but informed the club he will not be signing an extension. The two-time European champions have added Ferran Torres, Maghnes Akliouche and Mika Godts to their formidable attacking options this summer and have omitted Barcola from their matchday squads this season.

PSG signed Barcola for €45m from Lyon in 2023 and the winger has played a prominent role in the rise of the Champions League winners. But Luis Enrique’s preference for a front line of Désiré Doué, Ousmane Dembélé and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia in PSG’s biggest matches last season prompted Barcola to consider his options.

The arrival of Barcola – and sources insist it is not done yet – would make him the second-most expensive signing in Liverpool’s history behind the £125m Alexander Isak, but the club have still to land a replacement for Mohamed Salah on the right. Liverpool have had two bids rejected by Brighton for Yankuba Minteh and, despite enquiring over Ismaïla Sarr’s availability, have not made an offer for the Crystal Palace forward so far.

Cody Gakpo’s future at Liverpool will be in doubt should the club sign two wingers before the deadline. The Netherlands international has interest from Tottenham and Manchester City and Iraola admitted he could not guarantee Gakpo will remain a Liverpool player beyond Tuesday. “When the market is open you can not guarantee anything with anyone,” he said.

“I don’t know what is going to happen with any of our players. I cannot guarantee anything. You think I can smell who we are going to sign or what position but experience shows you that, if there is an opportunity on the last day, let’s take it.”

While Barcola and a replacement for Salah are Liverpool’s priorities for the remainder of the window, Iraola would like to strengthen in other areas given the long-term absences of the right-back Conor Bradley and striker Hugo Ekitike. “Ideally is the magic word,” Iraola said. “We don’t know what we can do but it’s true the priority has been mostly in the wide areas. Still we have four or five days. I am sure if we can improve other areas we will but I don’t know how the market is going to finish.

“You have to look at the overall picture. It’s not just in this position or the other We know from the beginning our demands. one. From the first day I arrived here I told you that it was wingers, especially because we lost Mo Salah, and then tricky situations with the players that have long-term injuries. We are probably down a player in some positions and those have been our main issues but if we can improve in other areas, we will.”

Sports.title: Spurs still paying price for a punishing World Cup and pre-season trip to Australia
Sports.content:
Jan Paul van Hecke was among those given an unwanted name-check by Roberto De Zerbi after Tottenham’s 3-0 defeat at Brentford on Saturday. Not at the right level physically, was the gist of the manager’s comments. De Zerbi also mentioned Marcos Senesi and Sandro Tonali, two of the club’s other new signings. Their condition had to come as no surprise. It certainly did not to De Zerbi.

Take the case of Van Hecke, for whom the summer months have been a whirlwind. A few bullet-points from his timeline are worth noting. 18 June: joins Spurs from Brighton for £52m; 30 June: knocked out of World Cup with the Netherlands after last-32 penalty shootout defeat to Morocco; 23 July: boards team flight with Spurs for pre-season tour to New Zealand and Australia. “It was a really short break, to be honest,” Van Hecke says. “But I didn’t want to miss anything in the pre-season. My first days [as a Spurs player] were in New Zealand and Australia.”

The centre-half had never been to New Zealand and Australia and he enjoyed the experience, getting a good feeling from the welcome there. Van Hecke was struck by the fans’ passion as well. That was the upside. The fallout from the downside continues to be felt. “Physical-wise, of course, it impacts your body,” he says. “I struggled for one or two weeks after and that’s not ideal. There are two sides. Normally you don’t go there and now you see that they also love football. That’s something good.”

Whose idea was such a far-flung tour in a World Cup summer? Definitely not De Zerbi’s. He inherited the schedule when he came to the club in late March and has done a fair bit of grumbling about it. “The trip was 25-26 hours,” De Zerbi said on Tuesday. “We played every three days. The day after [matches] we couldn’t work in the right condition.”

There appears to have been something of a quid pro quo arrangement with De Zerbi, who wanted to use the summer to close ranks and train. Nothing else. No travel. Just hard graft and tactical work. Spurs’ final game of the three on tour was against Chelsea in Sydney on 1 August. The club then arranged three further friendlies – against Getafe at the training ground in Enfield on 8 August before a double-header against Hoffenheim. Spurs played at their stadium against the German club on 15 August before hosting them at the training ground 24 hours later for a game with different players. De Zerbi was still not happy. “When we came back [to London] we couldn’t work immediately because there was a friendly game against Getafe,” he added.

Van Hecke did not play in the match against Auckland, or the first one in Australia against Sydney. He started against Chelsea. Then against Getafe and in the stadium fixture against Hoffenheim. His ratio of air miles to match minutes was high.

Senesi, who signed on a free transfer from Bournemouth on 1 July, did not go on tour after he played for Argentina in the World Cup final against Spain on 19 July. His first action for Spurs was in the stadium game against Hoffenheim. De Zerbi pitched him in from the start against Brentford alongside Van Hecke. It was logical that De Zerbi should lament Senesi’s level. And also that of Van Hecke.

What raised eyebrows was that he added Tonali to the mix. The Italian did not play at the World Cup after his country failed to qualify. He signed for Spurs from Newcastle for £92.5m on 6 July. The 26-year-old had a full pre-season, playing in virtually all of the games. The fact that De Zerbi did not consider Tonali fully ready for Brentford felt like the ultimate indictment of the club’s preparations.

De Zerbi left Tonali out of the squad for the 5-1 home win over Charlton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, along with Senesi, explaining that he preferred to put them through an intense training session on Tuesday so that they were better prepared for Saturday’s game against Newcastle, also at home. The fixture will carry extra significance for Tonali.

“Sando was in a plan to work with Marcos very strong to improve their physical condition,” De Zerbi said after Charlton. “Sandro has to work to feel better in terms of physical condition, but on Saturday he will play in the first XI.”

The tour threw up plenty of other complications. Another new signing, Mateus Fernandes, felt an injury when he got to Sydney, having played against Auckland. He did not feature again until the training ground match with Hoffenheim. Dominic Solanke picked up something against Chelsea and missed the remainder of the pre-season. Both players were fit enough only to be substitutes at Brentford. They started against Charlton.

View image in fullscreen Injuries and a hectic pre-season have given Roberto De Zerbi plenty to think about. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

What about Micky van de Ven? Van Hecke’s Dutch teammate travelled to New Zealand and Australia but he did not play there, in any of the subsequent pre-season games or against Brentford because of an injury. De Zerbi said last Friday that it had been sustained on tour. “I don’t know, the flight,” said De Zerbi. “I don’t know … something, not a big problem, but not right to work.”

De Zerbi brought Van de Ven on as a substitute against Charlton. Ditto Pedro Porro, who did not kick a ball in pre-season after winning the World Cup with Spain. Neither did he feature against Brentford. Destiny Udogie, who did not play in pre-season despite going on tour, was a substitute at Brentford and a starter against Charlton. He is playing catch-up. As is Rodrigo Bentancur, who was not a part of the tour after being granted extended leave after his World Cup exertions with Uruguay. He, too, was a substitute at Brentford and a starter against Charlton.

De Zerbi could enjoy the Charlton win even if there were caveats. Spurs were poor for the opening 30 minutes before they cut loose. The Charlton manager, Nathan Jones, made 10 changes to the team he sent out for the win at West Ham on Saturday. Everyone at Spurs knows Newcastle will present an altogether tougher challenge. It is time to dig deep.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Why the transfer window is actually a large collection of different windows
Sports.content:
THROUGH THE LOOKING GLASS

The transfer window isn’t an actual window, of course. In reality, it’s a large collection of different windows, with each club having one of their own, through which they peer longingly, occasionally flinging large quantities of cash money out of them like half-cut sailors on a ship coming into dock, and they’re all in various states of disrepair. For example, Tottenham have only recently prised theirs open – the previous occupant, Mr Levy, had deliberately painted over the seals – and all summer it’s been flapping in the breeze like the screen door of a haunted house. Manchester City meanwhile have removed the glass from their frames altogether, allowing the free movement of large expensive items safely through it in both directions. There are some officious-looking gentlemen with clipboards currently double-checking the structural integrity of that one. They say they’ll get back to us.

As for the window at Anfield, well, nobody’s been looking after that at all. State of it! Untended and covered in grime. Football Daily rubbed a small patch clear and peered through, only to see someone fast asleep at their desk, a passport and a one-way ticket to Saudi Arabia in one hand, clutched close to their chest. Someone else poked them with a stick, and eventually there was some reluctant movement. Seems a fee of just over £100m has been agreed with PSG for Bradley Barcola, with add-ons based on individual and team success that won’t happen if Liverpool’s other recent big-money purchases are anything to go by, so they won’t bring the fee up to £120m. Football Daily used a finger to scribble “CLEAN ME” and “YOU DO REALISE IT’S A RIGHT WINGER YOU DESPERATELY NEED?” in the dust on the pane and quietly moved along.

Chelsea meantime have completely redefined the whole concept of the window, replacing theirs with a revolving door. See it constantly turn, powered by steam generated by the hot mess that is late-stage capitalism, and on Thursday morning Liam Delap flew out of it. An unceremonious dispatch, Delap has been cashiered in borderline disgrace after scoring two goals in all competitions since his £30m move from Ipswich one year ago, and yet somehow Chelsea have managed to make a £15m profit by flipping him to Nottingham Forest, who would have legitimate grounds for complaint at the absurd fee had they not started this whole nonsense years ago by breaking the £1m barrier for Trevor Francis.

As Delap crashed clumsily through Forest’s window, sending shards of glass flying everywhere, Evangelos Marinakis grabbed a few planks of wood and quickly boarded it up, thus ensuring Morgan Gibbs-White still can’t flee. Meanwhile having finally thought it through, Football Daily concluded that things were far better, and way less tedious, when the transfer window was simply an overarching metaphor for the period during which clubs are permitted to exchange contracts for playing staff, as opposed to actual, well, y’know. Yes, we think we’ll go back to treating it like that, until the whole thing SLAMS SHUT and we can keep it closed for another four months.

“I don’t need a contract. I have a very successful career. I have taken care of my money. I can give this present to myself. To put that shirt on … for free because I wanted to help my club, my team, my city. It’s something that I wanted to do. It’s something that I am able to do and it’s something that makes me feel so proud to be able to be here just to help” – Ander Herrera explains why he has signed up to play for free for Real Zaragoza in the Spanish third tier.

View image in fullscreen Ander Herrera in his PSG days. Photograph: JE E/SIPA/Shutterstock

In the hope that the same trick works for me, in terms of improving my strike rate in getting letters to Football Daily published, I’m changing my name to Noble Francis” – Phil Taverner.

Sports.title: Dortmund best of the rest as Bundesliga clubs grasp at Bayern Munich’s coattails | Andy Brassell
Sports.content:
The Franz Beckenbauer Supercup has a modicum more intensity than most of its European equivalents. There are many reasons for this. The Bundesliga’s traditional season curtain-raiser pitting league champions against cup winners is not played on neutral territory, giving it the feeling of a domestic game with proper stakes.

German fans would also never accept it taking place on foreign soil, as the Borussia Dortmund managing director, Carsten Cramer, reiterated in clear terms over the course of the weekend. It feels like a match, rather than a showpiece.

It had one other factor to ratchet up the adrenaline this year. It was the sense the two teams most expect to be the season’s best, Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund, were the participants, with last term’s second-placed side hosting the champions. There was enough in the game to suggest Dortmund may be able inconvenience their rivals, as Bayern held on to win the season’s first trophy after BVB followed a thoroughly dominant first half from the visitors with a vastly improved second period.

But enough to create genuine jeopardy? That was harder to buy into. We all know what it takes for someone else to win the title in Germany: an exceptional team, such as Jürgen Klopp’s Borussia Dortmund or the Xabi Alonso-era Bayer Leverkusen, allied with a below-par Bayern. That second clause is far from being fulfilled.

For every action there is a reaction and in the past 15 years when Bayern have been domestically beaten it was met with a fierce response. So if Dortmund provoked Bayern to hit unimaginable levels with the 2013 treble, the same snap out of a deep funk has happened under Vincent Kompany. For Klopp’s wins in 2011 and 2012, read 2023 – when Dortmund all but handed Bayern their title back on the final day – and 2024, when Alonso’s Leverkusen finally took it away from them again. Once again, two years of fallibility was enough to make Bayern respond with force.

View image in fullscreen Ismaël Saibari lifts the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup trophy after Bayern Munich beat Borussia Dortmund. Photograph: Marvin Ibo Guengoer/GES/Getty Images

The leadership that has taken the champions there is key. Just as few would have imagined in spring 2012 that Jupp Heynckes would lead Bayern to virtual invincibility, there was not a queue of people scrambling to decree Kompany as the man to inspire the Rekordmeister to heights not reached since peak Pep Guardiola, but here we are.

Kompany has transformed the team in terms of intensity and culture and that they have signed only two senior players – but excellent fits in Nathaniel Brown, who scored the opener in the Super Cup, and Ismaël Saibari – shows how difficult they are to improve.

Harry Kane, whose season opens with Bayern campaigning hard for his Ballon d’Or candidacy, is symbolic of just how relentless this Bayern vintage is. “It’s always about sending a message,” he said of Bayern’s intentions going into Saturday’s match. “Our momentum is to keep pushing, to keep pushing each other and to see how far we can go.”

The sentiment among their Bundesliga rivals, both publicly and privately, is that keeping pace with Bayern is probably not a realistic aim. Dortmund have belatedly realised that spending on names to try to keep up is a flawed strategy. It has been a significant summer, shedding the big salaries of Niklas Süle, Julian Brandt and Karim Adeyemi. The young Greek pair of Konstantinos Karetsas and Giannis Konstantelias have arrived to re-energise their midfield, which will suit the demands of the coach, Niko Kovac.

Going young is a smart and overdue move and they showed in the Supercup that, even if they are at the foot of the title mountain, they at last have sturdy walking shoes and plenty of drinking water.

What we can expect from Leverkusen and RB Leipzig is a little less clear. For Leverkusen, the 2024 champions, failing to make the Champions League places last season was a failure, but it allowed them to let Kasper Hjulmand go, drawing a line under a chaotic season that began with Erik Ten Hag’s three-match reign.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This pre-season has been “more calm,” the sporting director, Simon Rolfes, said with some understatement, and even if Alejandro Grimaldo left for Atlético Madrid, life at BayArena is now stable. They retain their ambition under the new coach, Carles Martínez, and new signings – including bringing back Moussa Diaby from Saudi Arabia – have underlined that. Leipzig will participate in the Champions League, but a concrete aim is hard to define. They had planned to hold on to Yan Diomandé, but the money on offer from Real Madrid became too much to resist, with RB receiving more than six times the €20m they paid Leganès for him the year before. The return of Christopher Nkunku is bold, but signing a player who will be 29 in November is unlike them and it is worth recalling that bringing back Timo Werner, who had been a hero in his first spell at the club, backfired badly. The removal of Ole Werner as coach – sanctioned by Klopp before he took the Germany job – and his replacement with Martín Demichelis, who oversaw Mallorca’s relegation in May, is a risk. Another item for these clubs to consider could be the recent ruling by the Bundeskartellamt – the Federal Cartel Office – that the 50+1 rule is being applied correctly and justifiably by the Bundesliga in accordance with competition law. In short, this means 50+1 is here to stay and a genuine commitment to the principle, in terms of fans being represented more fully on the boards of clubs from corporate seed, could be demanded.

Stuttgart and Sebastian Hoeness will hope to prove they can compete in Bundesliga and Champions League simultaneously – the final frontier at the club for arguably the league’s most accomplished coach. With the transfer deadline in sight, the sporting director, Fabian Wohlgemuth, has largely kept an excellent squad together and added extra, youthful attacking punch in Dzenan Pejcinovic and Leo Sauer.

View image in fullscreen Dzenan Pejcinovic has joined an excellent squad at Stuttgart. Photograph: Axel Schmidt/Reuters

Freiburg, fresh from the experience of reaching an unprecedented Europa League final under Julian Schuster, have smartly invested some of the money from selling Johan Manzambi to Aston Villa to strengthen their squad. They could view this season’s Conference League as a legitimate target. Hoffenheim have spent all of the fee received for Bazoumana Touré as they return to the Champions League, while Eintracht Frankfurt are just glad to see the back of Albert Riera.

We are once again likely to see some big boys are probably going to be hanging around the lower reaches of the table again. Schalke, back after a three-year absence, forged a strong identity under Miron Muslic last year and are led by 40-year-old Edin Dzeko after he signed a new deal, but staying up is the main aim. Northern rivals Hamburg and Werder Bremen have bigger name strikers than imagined, but will need to nurse Terem Moffi and Nicklas Füllkrug, respectively, back to form.

Köln have benefited – at least in a sporting sense – from Saïd El Mala’s Dortmund move falling through and he becomes the first Effzeh player since Lukas Podolski to wear the No 10.

Many think they can already ink in first and last – Bayern and the first-timers Elversberg, representing a town of 13,000. But as BVB have already showed, a bit of tempo and youthful talent can shake up the expected order, even if only temporarily.

Sports.title: Manchester City target Iliman Ndiaye but Everton value forward at £80m
Sports.content:
Manchester City have identified Iliman Ndiaye as a potential target after the £75m departure of Sávio to Tottenham Everton value the wide forward in the region of £80m.

With Omar Marmoush also joining Spurs, on an initial season-long loan, Enzo Maresca wants to strengthen his attacking options. He is an admirer of Ndiaye, who has played 44 times for Senegal and is contracted to Everton until 2029.

Everton are interested in bringing Jack Grealish back from City after having him on loan last season. Grealish, also on Sunderland’s list of targets, is in the final year of his deal and Maresca suggested on Thursday the 30-year-old would leave.

“Jack is here until the day that he’s not here,” he said. “It’s my duty to try to help him to give us the best and then we’ll see in the next four-five days what happens.”

City agreed a €37.5m (£34m) deal for the Palmeiras winger Allan Elias on Monday, and are monitoring Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo.

Maresca said City were also aiming to add “one or two captains” before the transfer window closes on Tuesday night. This summer, City’s squad has lost the leadership and experience of Bernardo Silva, Rodri, John Stones and Nathan Aké.

Maresca has nominated Rúben Dias and Erling Haaland as captains, but wants to add more players who can fill the role. One the Italian has identified is Enzo Fernández, who has captained Chelsea.

Although Chelsea’s deadline of 14 August for a bid to be lodged passed without one, City are expected to move for the 25-year-old midfielder. The targeting of Fernández follows the departures of Rodri and Nico González.

Maresca spoke generally about leadership. “We have experienced players,” he said. “For sure, we have leaders. Now we need to wait four-five more days when the transfer window closes if we can add one or two more captains to Rúben and Erling.”

Matheus Nunes is a doubt for City’s trip to Crystal Palace on Friday.

Sports.title: Cribbed crest? Leyton Orient call out Wrexham for using familiar new badge
Sports.content:
Leyton Orient have criticised Wrexham’s owners, Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac, for putting a badge on their new kit that mirrors their own. Wrexham unveiled their new third strip on Wednesday; it is cream with a black collar and terracotta-orange detailing and received the Hollywood seal of approval with pictures of Mac and Reynolds modelling it on the club website.

But it was the badge that raised eyebrows as Wrexham deviated from their traditional crest of two red dragons facing inward, a golden football, the Prince of Wales feathers with a coronet and motto and Welsh flag colours. Instead, the badge was replaced with two wyverns or dragons facing each other over a football and looking remarkably like the crest Orient introduced in 1976 to incorporate the club’s links with the City of London and the Thames.

“What you playing at @VancityReynolds @RMcElhenney?,” posted Orient on social media, alongside a video of the former England manager Roy Hodgson using colourful language.

The wyvern is the defender of the Thames in mythology and with the sea, through the old Orient Shipping Company.

Sports.title: Wrexham called out by EFL club over alarmingly similar badge on third kit
Sports.content:
Wrexham called out by EFL club over alarmingly similar badge on third kit

Leyton Orient were not best impressed after Wrexham unveiled their new kit.

Hollywood co-owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney helped launch the Championship club's new third shirt.

2 Spot the difference between Leyton Orient's badge and the one on Wrexham's third kit? Credit: Getty

However, people noticed an immediate issue.

That is because the badge looks strikingly similar to Leyton Orient's.

"You appear to have nicked Orient’s badge," one person wrote on X.

Another added: "I think Orient need to send over a cease and desist letter considering you’ve ripped off our badge."

A third said: "When did Wrexham purchase Leyton Orient?"

Leyton Orient's response

The League One club had the perfect reply, posting an iconic Roy Hodgson meme.

The crest currently used by Orient dates from 1976 when a competition to design a new club crest was held in the Walthamstow Guardian newspaper.

Some have pointed out in the comments that Wrexham actually got there first.

The Welsh club's crest, with two dragons and a football between them, dates back to 1973 - three years before Orient's design.

This also resulted from a competition that was open to fans to submit their designs.

2 Wrexham have drawn their opening two Championship games of the season Credit: Getty

Wrexham's start so far

After narrowly missing out on the Championship play-offs last season, Phil Parkinson will be hoping he can go one better.

There is a better chance this season of reaching the Premier League too as those play-off places go down to eighth.

Wrexham have been aggressive in the transfer market to improve their squad this summer.

They have made five signings so far and are expected to have more incomings before the window closes on Tuesday.

Anthony Patterson joined for £8million from Sunderland, while defenders Danny Imray and Issa Kabore signed from Crystal Palace and Man City, respectively.

Midfielder Ben Whiteman was added from Preston, meanwhile left-back Jacques Ekomie came in from Ligue 1 club Angers.

The Red Dragons have drawn their opening two Championship games and face Birmingham on Friday night, with commentary live on talkSPORT2.

Sports.title: Chelsea set to sign 18-year-old prodigy in huge £40m deal
Sports.content:
Chelsea are closing in on the capture of a second Atalanta defender after agreeing a deal to sign Honest Ahanor, talkSPORT understands.

The Blues are set to reunite the 18-year-old Italian with their new right-back Marco Palestra, who arrived from the Serie A side in July.

3 Atalanta rejected a bid from Brighton for Ahanor earlier this summer Credit: Getty

Ahanor made 28 league appearances for Atalanta in his maiden campaign at the club, having joined from Genoa last summer.

Chelsea agree £40m Honest Ahanor transfer

He now looks to be on the move for a second successive summer, after Chelsea reportedly struck a deal in the region of £40million.

Ahanor has been given permission to travel for a medical and complete a move to Stamford Bridge.

The report adds that personal terms are already in place on a long-term contract for the two-cap Italy international. It remains to be seen what Chelsea's long-term thinking for the player is.

Who is Honest Ahanor?

Atalanta's No.69 came through Genoa’s academy and rose through the ranks to make six appearances for Il Grifone's first-team.

The versatile defender quickly established himself at his new club following his arrival last summer, having made 18 starts across his 35 appearances in the 2025/26 campaign.

Ahanor, who has primarily been used as the left-sided defender in a back three, can also play at left-back and across the midfield.

Atalanta's sporting director Cristiano Giuntoli confirmed earlier this week that the club would ‘evaluate’ any proposals they received in the final few days of the window when asked about Ahanor's future.

"Right now, there’s a week to go [until the transfer window closes]," he said during Atalanta’s press conference to unveil Eljif Elmas on Tuesday.

"I won’t deny that we have some players who are attracting strong interest, but no offers have arrived. We’ll evaluate them if they arrive."

3 The 18-year-old has been given permission to travel for a medical Credit: Getty

Chelsea transfers

Ahanor now seems destined to become part of Xabi Alonso's defensive overhaul at Chelsea, which begun with Palestra's arrival.

In addition to the Atalanta duo, the Blues have also signed Maxence Lacroix from Crystal Palace and Pep Chavarria from Rayo Vallecano.

talkSPORT understands Chelsea are in talks with Aston Villa over Emiliano Martinez, who is available for as little as £8.6m.

Eslewhere, the club have already added Morgan Rogers, Geovany Quenda, Valentin Barco, Emmanuel Emegha, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to their extensive first-team options.

Sports.title: UEFA to launch criminal proceedings against Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
UEFA is preparing to begin criminal proceedings against FIFA President Gianni Infantino, talkSPORT understands.

It comes after Infantino failed with his proposal to sell off stakes in FIFA competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors.



2 Infantino's FIFA Forward Enterprise project backfired badly Credit: Getty

UEFA submit 60-page document

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs explained: "UEFA has sent a 60-page discovery claim to the United States District Court in Florida as it prepares to take criminal action against Gianni Infantino in Switzerland related to the FIFA President's failed privatisation plans known as FIFA Forward Enterprise.

"The petition, seen by talkSPORT, asks for authorisation for subpoenas for two US-based departments of FIFA, FIFA Americas and the 2026 World Cup, in order to gain the production of documents and communications as UEFA compiles a case against Infantino and hopes in doing so it forces him out of the FIFA presidency."

Infantino's controversial plans sparked widespread outrage throughout football, with FIFA member associations steadily withdrawing their support for the 56-year-old.



UEFA also called for a boycott of FIFA tournaments, though they are reportedly set to drop this after being reassured that Infantino won't stage a repeat of his proposal.

The Irish FA recently joined the list of national federations going public with their opposition to Infantino continuing as FIFA president.



Formerly Secretary General of UEFA, Infantino was appointed FIFA President in 2016 and is up for re-election next year.

Infantino's U-turn

After backing down on FIFA Forward Enterprise at the end of July, Infantino said in a statement: "Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place."



The saga also drew criticism from high-ranking FIFA officials, with Infantino's senior adviser Carlos Cordeiro resigning.

"I cannot stand by while FIFA considers selling a stake in the World Cup," Cordeiro said.

Meanwhile, FIFA's chief operating officer, Kevin Lamour, derided FIFA Forward Enterprise as a solo endeavour on Infantino's part.

2 Infantino has come under intense scrutiny in recent weeks Credit: AFP



"It is the project of one person," Lamour said. "Not only must this project not go ahead… but the time has now come for football political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.

"And if that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I'll sleep well tonight."

However, other FIFA members have continued to stand by Infantino.

They include 2030 World Cup co-hosts Morocco and beaten 2026 finalists Argentina, who saw three players banned for their part in the ugly scenes at full-time of their defeat to Spain.

FIFA will hold its presidential election at the 77th FIFA Congress in Rabat, next March.



Wenger for President?

talkSPORT's Simon Jordan recently tipped Arsene Wenger, currently FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development, to succeed Infantino.

"If you want the best for the sport, Infantino should step aside and let Arsene Wenger run it," the former Crystal Palace chairman said.

Wenger himself said Infantino's U-turn on FIFA Forward Enterprise was 'absolutely necessary and beyond question'.

Sports.title: Man United enter talks with new club over Joshua Zirkzee exit
Sports.content:
Man United enter talks with new club over Joshua Zirkzee exit

Fiorentina have entered talks with Manchester United over a deal for Joshua Zirkzee, talkSPORT understands.

The Italian side are keen to bring the Netherlands international back to Serie A before the transfer window closes.

3 Fiorentina are in talks with United over a deal for Zirkzee Credit: AFP

However, an official bid has yet to be placed for the 25-year-old forward.

Zirkzee was an unused substitute in United's Premier League opening weekend defeat to Hull City last Saturday.

Matheus Cunha was preferred to lead the line at the MKM Stadium before being replaced by Benjamin Sesko in the second half.

Zirkzee's United future

It leaves Zirkzee's future under Michael Carrick in the balance amid Fiorentina's interest in a move.

The striker's current Old Trafford deal expires in 2029 having arrived from Bologna two years ago.

Zirkzee has since scored just nine goals in 75 appearances across all competitions for the club.

His last strike for United came in a Premier League meeting with Wolves back in December.

The trip to Hull had followed an impressive pre-season for Zirkzee, who was not included in the Netherlands' World Cup squad.

Despite scoring once in six caps for the Oranje, his last call-up came back in November 2024.

Zirkzee was on target twice for United during the summer, including a goal and an assist in a 5-0 win over Rosenborg.

3 Carrick opted not to use Zirkzee at any point against Hull despite the player's impressive pre-season Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

He also opened the scoring in their clash with Leeds United in Dublin on August 12.

The Red Devils won the match on penalties following a 1-1 draw at Croke Park.

Zirkzee in Italy

talkSPORT previously revealed Roma had targeted a January loan move for Zirkzee.

However, he ultimately remained with the Red Devils for the second half of the campaign.

A long-awaited return to Italy could now be offered by Fiorentina.

Zirkzee spent two seasons with Bologna prior to his £36million move to United.

3 Fiorentina are yet to launch an official bid for Zirkzee with talks ongoing Credit: Getty

During that time, he scored 13 goals and added seven assists in 53 Serie A appearances.

The former Bayern Munich man also had a loan spell at Parma back in 2021.

Sports.title: Matteo Guendouzi must ‘suffer the consequences’ as Simon Jordan urges owners to issue sanction
Sports.content:
Matteo Guendouzi must feel the weight of the football laws for his 'antagonistic' behaviour at a bad-tempered Champions League clash.

Fenerbahce, who Guendouzi plays for, booked their place in the league phase of the Champions League with a 2-1 win on Wednesday night in France, triumphing 3-2 on aggregate – and Guendouzi later sparked chaotic scenes as he celebrated by baiting the Lyon fans.



2 Guendouzi celebrated right in the faces of the Lyon fans Credit: Getty

Guendouzi previously played for Lyon's bitter rivals Marseille with the former Arsenal midfielder's actions angering not only the supporters but also the Lyon players, who took him to task on the pitch.

Some club officials were also involved in what descended into a mass brawl.

Jordan slams 'antagonising' Guendouzi

And talkSPORT's Jordan feels Guendouzi should be punished above anyone else for his part in the post-match pandemonium.



Speaking on talkSPORT's White and Jordan, the ex-Crystal Palace chairman said: "People are responsible for their own behaviour, so everybody is culpable and everybody in terms of the professionals on the field – the players – and the support staff that have got involved should have a consequence for it.

"But he [Guendouzi] should have the primary consequence because without his provocation, without his antagonising nature, without his ridiculous over-egging of the pudding and baiting [the situation wouldn't have boiled over].



"The fans are not professional footballers. The key is in the title: he's a professional footballer that has a responsibility to behave himself within the confines of reasonable levels of behaviour.

"I get it that footballers get a lot of antagonistic comments made to them on the field and a lot of abuse, and when it comes to abuse of a racial nature of other natures, that's discriminatory and there's no tolerance of that.



"But when it comes to abuse about who you play for and those sort of things, I think that just goes with the territory. And that's what makes you a professional footballer, getting paid £100,000 a week."

Could Guendouzi receive Argentina-style punishment?

Asked by Jim White whether Guendouzi should face a similar punishment to the Argentina players slapped with lengthy bans for their part in the ugly scenes at the end of the World Cup final, Jordan responded: "I don't know the menu that they can pull from in terms of sanctioning him.

"But he can't behave like that. He can't create and curate that, and he has to suffer a consequence for it because that's unnecessary.

2 UEFA are bound to take a dim view of Guendouzi's inflammatory behaviour Credit: Getty



"Again, I price into my thinking about what people should have to endure on a football field.

"And if you told these kids, 'You're going to become a multimillionaire footballer, but people are going to shout a few nasty hurty words to you on a football field – are you going to be able to cope with that?', they'd all say yes.

"And when it comes on top, they're all indignant about what they have to listen to. In this instance, he's been a provocateur.

"He is antagonising the fans because of a rivalry between two football clubs that have very little to do with him and he is creating a set of behaviour which is unbecoming of a professional footballer on a football field."



What would Jordan do?

White asked Jordan what he would do if he were the president of Fenerbahce, to which Jordan said he would want to take matters into his own hands.

Jordan continued: "I have to be honest, if he was my player, I'd have a different relationship with him than the players that I don't have a relationship with.

"So, I would always want to look after my players and want to get in front of a sanction. I'd want to smack him myself and put him in his place.

"But I'd want to try and sanction him in a way that I chose fit and to mitigate what the federation or the authorities might do because I want to say to the force: 'I've got it; I've dealt with him'."

Sports.title: Aston Villa vs Arsenal LIVE commentary: Konsa prepares for Villa Park return following summer switch
Sports.content:
Aston Villa vs Arsenal LIVE commentary: Konsa prepares for Villa Park return following summer switch

Arsenal head to Aston Villa on Monday as they look to make it back-to-back wins to start the Premier League season, live on talkSPORT.

The Gunners kicked off their top-flight title defence in style with a 3-0 win over newly promoted Coventry City.



4 Martin Odegaard opened his account for the season and looked much fitter than previous years Credit: Getty

Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard all scored as Mikel Arteta's side made the dream start to the campaign and played some brilliant football.

For Aston Villa, it couldn't have been much worse as Unai Emery's men were dismantled 4-0 by Brighton.

They conceded four in the first half and had Joao Gomes sent off, while Ollie Watkins didn't play.



The striker is looking to join Saudi Arabian side Al-Ahli and took no part in the contest.

Despite this, Villa will still hope to replicate their 2-1 win over Arsenal from last year.



How to follow Aston Villa vs Arsenal

This Premier League game will take place on Monday, August 31.

Kick-off at Villa Park is scheduled for 8pm.

talkSPORT's live and exclusive coverage of the match will be hosted by Adrian Durham.

Commentary comes from Sam Matterface and former Fulham midfielder Danny Murphy.



4 Konsa has left Villa to join Arsenal in the latest departure from the Midlands club

4 Emery couldn't believe what he was watching as his team collapsed Credit: Getty

Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app, whilst talkSPORT is also available to watch on Samsung TV Plus.



Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Aston Villa vs Arsenal team news

Villa could decide to hand Zion Suzuki a debut in goal in place of Marco Bizot.

Matteo Ruggeri came off the bench for his debut and he'll be pushing for a first start.



The home side will also hope to have Nicolas Jackson signed in time to lead the line.

A £65million deal with Chelsea has been agreed, and he should be taking his medical and completing the move over the weekend.

Emery still can't call upon Johan Manzambi, and he joins Amadou Onana, Brian Madjo and Leon Bailey on the sidelines.

Arsenal are likely to hand Ezri Konsa his debut against his former team.



The centre-back completed a £50m move from Villa to Arsenal earlier this month.

Jurrien Timber is still not back in training and William Saliba is out for a few months with a back injurry.

They will hope that Guimaraes is back from a niggle to make his Premier League debut.

4 Guimaraes missed the Coventry match due to injury Credit: Getty



Record season for Arsenal awaits?

It might be very early days, but Adrian Durham has backed Arsenal to win the title by a record total.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, he said: "It feels like it's going to be so, so easy.

"I believed Arsenal would break the record for the points gap at the top of the table at the end of the season.

"They won't just win the title, they'll win it by miles. I think it could be a 20-plus points margin.



"There literally is no competition for Arsenal.

"They were so good last season and they've strengthened this season. I can only see one winner."

Sports.title: Atletico Madrid hold secret talks with Arsenal over Julian Alvarez sale
Sports.content:
Atletico Madrid sent a delegation to London last week to speak to Arsenal about selling Julian Alvarez, talkSPORT understands.

The LaLiga club are adamant they won’t sanction a transfer to Barcelona, and have since published a board statement confirming this position.

3 Alvarez has expressed his desire to leave Atletico Credit: Getty

Atleti sources had tried to paint the visit to London as for exploratory talks for Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson, however, is set to join Aston Villa from Chelsea.

Sources have told talkSPORT Atleti directly informed Arsenal they would consider offers for Alvarez in excess of £120m.

Arsenal are prepared to bid in the final days of the window if Alvarez decides to join.

A loan has also been discussed due to Arsenal considering whether Alvarez is willing to commit fully.

Alvarez has missed two days of training in an increasingly tense situation between player and club.

The official reason cited for the Argentina forward's absence is illness.

Atletico Madrid statement

The Spanish club released a statement on Thursday flat out refusing to sell to Barcelona.

It read: “Atlético de Madrid is open to standard transfer market negotiations when conducted in a professional, ethical and respectful manner.

“We fully stand behind the club’s previously communicated position that FC Barcelona failed to meet these requirements and, as a result, there will not be any negotiation and there is zero consideration of an Alvarez transfer to Barcelona.”

3 Alvarez is one of the most coveted stars in world football right now Credit: Getty

It also added a pointed message to Alvarez himself: “Atlético de Madrid trust that our player will understand the decision and will remain focused on helping the club achieve its goals, just as he has done during the two seasons he has been defending our colours.”

Atletico signed the 26-year-old in the summer of 2024 from Man City in a deal worth up to £82m.

He won the treble at City, scoring 36 goals in 103 games for the club.

Since joining Atletico, he has 49 strikes in 107 outings.

Julian Alvarez verdict

Speaking to talkSPORT, The Athletic reporter Dermot Corrigan said: “He’s played an awful lot of football over the last four years or so. He's played almost every summer, back from when he was at Man City, he played World Cups, won the World Cup with Argentina, played in the Olympic Games.

“There was a little feeling last year that he wasn't 100 per cent fit, but when the biggest games came around in the Champions League, he played and he scored some tremendous goals against Spurs, he was brilliant.

3 Alvarez has made clear he wants to leave Atletico with Arsenal his sole option Credit: Getty

“Against Barca, he was brilliant in the Champions League.

“Whereas in La Liga, week to week, sometimes he wasn't played, sometimes he didn't look quite, I wouldn't say he wasn't quite up for it, but he wasn't as focused maybe on the La Liga games, or Atletico weren't as focused on the La Liga games, because they were out of the title race so early last season.

“So the numbers don't look great, but I'd say he's a really quality player. He's a clutch player, he's a guy who stands up in the big moments, he started the World Cup as well for Argentina.

“When they needed a goal, he scored that tremendous goal to get them through in the knockout rounds. I think he's a great player.

“Whether he's £150m, it's hard to put prices on players these days, but I think he is worth it.”

Sports.title: Omar Marmoush deal ‘certain’ to trigger instant exit for Tottenham star
Sports.content:
Omar Marmoush's arrival at Tottenham Hotspur is bad news for one of the club's current forwards.

That is according to talkSPORT's Alan Brazil and Ally McCoist, who believe Richarlison is now a 'certainty' to leave Spurs this summer.



3 Richarlison is a 'certainty' to leave Spurs according to Brazil and McCoist Credit: Getty

Marmoush has finally completed a transfer to north London from Manchester City.

The Egyptian forward has moved to the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on a season-long loan with an obligation to buy.

Once made permanent, Spurs will pay an initial £50million plus up to £10million in add-ons.



However, his arrival could spell the end of Richarlison's time at Tottenham with the transfer deadline fast approaching.

The 29-year-old is into the final year of his current contract having joined the club from Everton in 2022.



Premier League sides have until 11pm on Tuesday to conclude their summer transfer business.

Will Richarlison leave Spurs?

Brazil and McCoist reacted to Marmoush' move to Spurs live on Wednesday's talkSPORT Breakfast show.



The former believes it spells the end of Richarlison's time at the club, admitting: "I think Richarlison is a certainty to leave."

His co-host agreed, with McCoist replying: "Yes, I would guess that would be the case."

Brazil then added: "He looks a moody git doesn't he? He's really moody, like the whole world's against him.

3 Marmoush has joined Spurs on loan from City with an obligation to buy Credit: Getty



"Sometimes he looks as if he's like, 'I don't care,' and then other times he can be brilliant, but he's gone."

Meanwhile, McCoist explained: "I think he's leaving. I don't think there's any doubt about that, I think he's going to go to pastures new."

Richarlison at Spurs

Richarlison has scored 32 goals in 134 appearances since joining Spurs four years ago.

He was part of the side which ended their 17-year wait for a trophy by winning the Europa League in 2025.



Speculation surrounding his future comes just days after he started their opening weekend defeat to Brentford.

Dominic Solanke replaced Richarlison in attack for Roberto De Zerbi's side during their 3-0 away loss on Saturday.

3 Richarlison has entered the final year of his current Spurs deal Credit: Getty

As for Marmoush, he has 10 goals and five assists in 37 Premier League outings for City.



Since arriving at the Etihad Stadium from Eintracht Frankfurt in January 2025, he has also won both the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

Sports.title: Latest on Manchester City and Arsenal's interest in Iliman Ndiaye as Reiss Nelson's Gunners contract is terminated - and Tottenham confirm Omar Marmoush: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Man United youngster heading out on loan Manchester United are set to send academy midfielder Dan Gore on loan to Luton Town. Daily Mail Sport understands that following multiple offers from EFL clubs, Gore is expected to head to Kenilworth Road on loan for the remainder of the season. The 21-year-old, who was handed his United first team debut in 2023, starred in League One for Rotherham United last season, winning their Player of the Season award, and has been identified by Luton Town boss Jack Wilshere for a promotion bid this time around. Manchester United are set to send academy midfielder Dan Gore (left) on loan to Luton Town Gore did not feature for United’s Under-21s on Monday night in their 5-0 win over Ipswich Town as his future was handled before Tuesday’s deadline. The youngster left a good impression on first team coaches with Jonathan Woodgate among those on Michael Carrick’s staff to take a liking to him in training. Manchester United are continuing to navigate approaches for fellow academy players Toby Collyer, Harry Amass, Diego Leon, Jaydan Kamason, and Jayce Fitzgerald. EXCLUSIVE BY NATHAN SALT Nelson to leave Arsenal Arsenal have agreed to terminate the contract of forward Reiss Nelson by mutual consent. The 26-year-old has recently been discussing a £3million move to West Ham but the agreement with Arsenal allows to have broader options. Nelson had 12 months left on his deal. Newcastle target training separately Lille coach Davide Ancelotti has confirmed Newcastle United target Mathias Fernandez-Pardo is training separately as he awaits a move to the Premier League. Ancelotti said: 'We made the decision that he wouldn't train with the group until the end of the transfer window and until his situation is resolved.' Lille coach Davide Ancelotti has confirmed Newcastle United target Mathias Fernandez-Pardo is training separately Newcastle are offering around £30m for the 21-year-old Belgium forward. Chelsea reach agreement over Ahanor... Honest! Chelsea have reached agreement with Atalanta to sign Italy international defender Honest Ahanor. The two clubs have struck a fee of £40million with personal terms in place on a long-term contract. The 18-year-old has been given permission to travel for a medical and complete a move to Stamford Bridge. He is expected to go out on loan, as reported in yesterday's Daily Mail Sport. Marmoush completes Spurs switch Omar Marmoush has joined Tottenham on a season-long loan from Manchester City, following team-mate Savio to north London. MATT BARLOW Villa ramp up Leao pursuit Aston Villa have sent a delegation to Milan to negotiate the loan signing of Rafael Leao, who also has an offer from Galatasaray. The Villa party were expected to hold talks today with AC Milan, with super agent Jorge Mendes involved in proceedings. Leao would cost an initial £6.9million loan fee which would become a £37m deal next summer if certain conditions are met. Rafael Leao is being pursued by Aston Villa and Galatasaray this summer Meanwhile, Ollie Watkins is expected in Riyadh on Friday to complete his £51m move to Al Hilal. Daily Mail Sport understands the England forward is due to be presented by the Saudi club as their latest signing in the next 24 hours. TOM COLLOMOSSE Ndiaye pursuit latest Manchester City appreciate Iliman Ndiaye but he has three years left on contract at Everton and is valued around £80m. Arsenal are also among his admirers while he has already turned down Al Hilal as he wanted to remain in the Premier League. Seelt seals Swans deal Sunderland defender Jenson Seelt is joining Swansea on a season-long loan deal. The 23-year-old centre-back has agreed a new four-year deal with Sunderland before making the move to Wales. Zirkzee's Italian job Manchester United are in talks with Fiorentina over the potential loan and sale of striker Joshua Zirkzee. The Italian club are willing to offer a £4m loan fee with buy option for the 25-year-old and talks are ongoing. Zirkzee has also had interest from Juventus, Napoli and a check call from Aston Villa as interest becomes more serious towards the close of the window. Palacios heading to Ipswich Ipswich are finalising paperwork for Bayer Leverkusen midfielder Exequiel Palacios who has completed his medical ahead of a £23.5m move. If all goes to plan, he could be confirmed in the next 24 hours, with Ipswich set to pay £19.4m plus add-ons. Hornets buzzing around Lascelles Watford are in talks to sign Jamaal Lascelles. The 32-year-old former Newcastle United captain was at Leicester City last season in a short term contract and is available as a free agent. Delap signs for Forest Liam Delap has sealed a £45million move to Nottingham Forest and could make his debut against Liverpool this weekend. Despite a poor season at Chelsea, Forest have chosen to focus on Delap's strong campaign for Ipswich and handed Chelsea an instant £15m profit - even though Delap scored only three goals for the Blues. Liam Delap has joined Forest after a difficult spell with Chelsea Forest boss Oliver Glasner has been desperate for a mobile No9 to allow Igor Jesus to operate in a different role. Delap will be expected to make an instant impact after Forest lost twice at home to Leeds in the space of four days. TOM COLLOMOSSE Tractor Boys keen on Tammy Ipswich are in talks to sign Aston Villa striker Tammy Abraham on loan. Villa are signing Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and have made approaches for Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta and Bayer Leverkusen's Christian Kofane while also making an offer for AC Milan winger Rafael Leao. Abraham signed for Villa for £18m in January scored three goals in four starts and 13 substitute appearances. Ipswich want to strengthen several positions before the deadline. Elliott eyeing Italian escape Liverpool midfielder Harvey Elliott is attracting interest from Italian sides Napoli and Lazio. The 23-year-old suffered a disappointing loan at Aston Villa last season stymied by the fact the deal became an obligation to buy at £35m if he made ten appearances. Unai Emery chose not to select him after a handful of games and admitted that it affected the England U21 international. Napoli and Lazio are interested in moves for Harvey Elliott He made just nine appearances and scored one goal last season though still finished with a Europa League winners medal albeit as an unused substitute. Though interest is expected over the next four days, Liverpool have still to receive a formal enquiry for Elliott. Barcola nearing Liverpool switch Liverpool are closing on a deal worth £120million for Paris Saint Germain forward Bradley Barcola. The deal is still to be completed but negotiations are continuing on a £100m fee with £20m in add-ons. Read the full story here. Tigers chasing Thomas Hull have made a revised bid for Stoke 'crossing machine' Sorba Thomas. The Tigers have already had a £7m offer rejected for the Wales international winger with Stoke looking for around £10m. Thomas was Stoke player of the year and made it into the divisional team of the year last season, contributing 13 assists, 10 goals, plus a couple of forced own goals. Indeed, analysts identified that 26-year-old Thomas supplied 410 crosses in his 45 league matches. The next highest in the Championship was Millwall's Femi Azeez with 294. He added to his tally last night as Stoke took on Hull in the Carabao Cup only to lose on penalties. Afterwards Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic, quizzed on his interest, said: 'I know everything about Sorba Thomas from the Championship, he's a difference maker, and he's a very good player.' Hull have also enquired about Fabio Carvalho at Brentford but they want the midfielder to stay. The Premier League new boys have agreed to sign Union Berlin forward Ilyas Ansah for around £21m. The Germany Under-21 international is undergoing a medical today. The Tigers are also discussing a loan for Roma striker Robinio Vaz, 19. Hull close on Nice star Nice forward Mohamed Ali Cho has completed his Hull medical. The former Everton and Paris Saint Germain prospect, 22, can play anywhere across the front line. The deal is worth up to £15.4m. Celtic consider Johnstone move Celtic are understood to be considering a move for experienced Wolves goalkeeper Sam Johnstone as they assess their options following their disastrous exit from the Champions League. The Scottish champions suffered one of the most damaging European defeats in their recent history on Tuesday night, incredibly surrendering a four-goal aggregate advantage to lose 5-4 to LASK and miss out on the Champions League league phase for a second successive season. Johnstone has emerged as a potential option. The 33-year-old England international is at Wolves but his future at Molineux is increasingly uncertain following the club's relegation to the Championship and subsequent changes to their goalkeeping department. Johnstone underwent shoulder surgery towards the end of last season, which ruled him out of the final matches of the campaign and disrupted his pre-season. However, he has been back training for several weeks, has regained full movement in the shoulder and is effectively back to full fitness. Despite his return to fitness, there are significant doubts over whether Johnstone features in new Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto's long-term plans. Jose Sa returned to the side following his involvement at the World Cup, while Wolves have moved to agree a £1.3million deal for Sporting Lisbon goalkeeper Joao Virginia and are in talks to bring back John Ruddy, another indication that the goalkeeping order at Molineux is changing. Although Dan Bentley has recently departed for Coventry City, Wolves have openly spoken about wanting another goalkeeper and would be willing to allow Johnstone to leave. The arrival of Virginia leaves Johnstone facing an uncertain battle for football and little evidence of a long-term future at Wolves, potentially opening the door for Celtic. Johnstone would bring considerable experience to Celtic Park. The former Manchester United academy goalkeeper has made more than 350 senior appearances during spells with West Bromwich Albion, Crystal Palace, Aston Villa and Wolves, while he has also represented England at senior level. At 33, he could offer Celtic an experienced and proven presence at a time when the club are looking for greater stability following the extraordinary collapse against LASK. With the transfer deadline approaching and Johnstone now nearing complete match fitness, it could be a situation that develops quickly. Celtic need a response after their Champions League humiliation and Johnstone needs regular football. A move to Glasgow could potentially suit both parties. Wanted man Morato Nottingham Forest defender Morato is wanted by Roma on loan. Forest are looking at Fiorentina right back Dodo after Celta Vigo halted talks for Javi Rueda. Saints explore Ward-Prowse return Southampton are exploring a deal to bring Hammers midfielder James Ward-Prowse back to St Mary's. They have already agreed a £3.8m deal with Augsburg for defender Keven Schlotterbeck. The 29-year old centre back underwent a medical yesterday.
