World.title: Croatian Firefighters Receive New vehicles for Extinguishing Forest Fires
World.content:
August the 27th, 2026 – Croatian firefighters have received six new, highly specialised modern vehicles for extinguishing forest fires.

A ceremony for the handover of new vehicles for extinguishing forest fires was held yesterday at the State Firefighting School in Zagreb. Index reports that the attendees included Chief Fire Commander Slavko Tucaković, county fire commanders and presidents of the firefighting associations of the counties receiving the vehicles, Buzet Mayor Damir Kajin, and representatives of the firefighting units to which the vehicles were allocated.

The six new specialised firefighting vehicles for extinguishing forest fires were financed from funds for the general-purpose functions of forests (OKFŠ). Those funds are distributed through the competent ministry in cooperation with the Croatian Firefighting Association.

a total of 78 new vehicles have been ordered

Chief Fire Commander Slavko Tucaković said that continuous investment in firefighting equipment further strengthens the operational capabilities of Croatian firefighters.

“By distributing these brand new vehicles, we’re raising the operational readiness of units not only for extinguishing outdoor fires, but also for a range of other sorts of interventions. These vehicles will immediately be put into operational use. Previously allocated vehicles have already been used on major fires on Korčula and near Lokva Rogoznica,” said Chief Fire Commander Tucaković, emphasising that the vehicles were built according to the requirements of fire commanders in the field.

where in croatia will they be put into function?

These vehicles are modernly equipped firefighting vehicles designed entirely for extinguishing forest fires and interventions in very demanding terrain. They have 4×4 drives, large water tanks, a fire pump and additional equipment for work in the most difficult conditions. A total of 40 vehicles with 2,500-litre water tanks and 38 vehicles with 5,000-litre tanks have been ordered. Today, five larger-capacity vehicles and one smaller-capacity vehicle were handed over.

The new vehicles were received by the Public Fire Brigade of Petrinja, the Public Fire Brigade of Buzet, the Public Fire Brigade of Imotski, the Public Fire Brigade of Županja, the Senj Volunteer Fire Department and the Brestovac Volunteer Fire Department.

World.title: Croatian Fires Often Occur on Overgrown, Neglected Private Land
World.content:
August the 27th, 2026 – Croatian fires often occur on overgrown and neglected private land where it’s difficult or impossible for Croatian Forests (Hrvatske šume) to enter and deal with the situation.

Large fires have become a European reality and no longer pose a threat only to the extreme south of Europe. As never before, fires have also hit the United Kingdom, the continental part of France and Germany. Marija Brnic reports for Poslovni that there have been fires up in Scandinavia as well, and in conditions of increasingly frequent extreme heatwaves they represent a greater threat than before for a far larger number of countries. The authorities have duly recognised this, as a joint defence has already been established, so that unlike earlier times, member states help one another by sending firefighting teams and firefighting fleets.

According to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), forest fires already reached a historic record last year – more than one million hectares of forest burned within the EU back in 2025. This year, according to data from the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre, as of the first week of August, 506 thousand hectares of forest area had burned, which is a third more than in the same period of the most devastating 2025.

Since the recovery of a destroyed forest ecosystem is measured in decades compared with agricultural crops or buildings, the question arises of what to do with these areas, and how this changes the picture on the timber raw material market. As of the first week of August, 506 thousand hectares of forest area had burned – a third more than in the same period of the most devastating 2025.

it’s still too early to make educated estimates

These questions are also relevant at the Croatian level, although, fortunately and thanks to a well-organised fire defence, the areas burned so far are still below the record levels of 2017 and the devastating 2022. By mid-August, 9.6 thousand hectares had been affected by fire.

Croatian Forests were asked for their estimates of damage to forested areas under their management that were affected by fires, and what the ratio of affected areas is compared with the previous year. They revealed that it is too early for any estimates; more concrete information will only be possible after the end of the fire season. However, they significantly emphasised that in the largest fire this year, the one in the wider Omiš area, only about ten percent of the total burned area was under the management of Croatian Forests.

As for the rehabilitation of the fire-affected areas, they explain that the law provides that it must be carried out no later than two growing seasons after the fire occurred. They are responsible for rehabilitating areas owned by the state, and they carry it out mainly independently or by engaging external subcontractors. The first step, if it concerns so-called high forest, is the extraction of timber mass, followed by preparation for the replanting of trees, which is done purposefully, in accordance with the adaptation of the tree species to the particular terrain.

However, some forest areas also regenerate on their own, especially those under pine trees, because during a fire the cones practically explode and disperse seed up to about ten metres. This brings us to the increasingly frequent and louder public questioning of replacing the flammable Aleppo pine with another tree species. Europe, precisely because of fires and climate change, is intensively considering abandoning conifers and switching to mixed and more resistant deciduous forests.

changes are unfortunately not likely

As for changes along Croatia’s long, heavily irregular coastal area, this is not currently likely. Experts have long pointed out that on karst and rock, where there is no fertile soil, deciduous trees cannot survive, and that the Aleppo pine is precisely suitable because it has extremely modest requirements. Moreover, it is the best at creating conditions for the start of humus production. That is also the reason why on the areas affected by fires that are under Croatian Forests, a rapid change of tree species is not likely.

“Given the conditions we constantly encounter, the pioneer species, in this case the Aleppo pine, simply does not manage to perform its primary function because of fires – creating conditions for the successful growth of other species. Unfortunately, we find it increasingly difficult to wait the sufficient number of years that are approximately needed for that process of conversion into mixed forests, because fires due to the climate and human behaviour have become ever more frequent and destructive,” they emphasise from Croatian Forests, reminding that 90 percent of them are caused by human negligence and carelessness or malicious intent.

Among other things, they note that fires often start from neglected and overgrown agricultural areas in private ownership, for which they are not responsible and which they are not allowed to enter, and which are very often overgrown precisely with Aleppo pine that has not been maintained there and has no firebreaks.

World.title: How do Croatian Fuel Prices Compare to the Rest of the EU?
World.content:
August the 27th, 2026 – Croatian fuel prices have been up and down like a yo-yo, but just how do they compare to those across the rest of the EU?

Energy expert Jasminko Umićević assessed that Croatia is not facing a fuel shortage, but warns that high prices could persist. Drivers in Croatia are once again paying more for fuel as of Tuesday. However, Eurostat data show that the rise in fuel prices over the past year was still milder than the European Union average. Diesel in Croatia rose by 14 percent, and petrol by eight percent.

Poslovni reports that according to data issued for July 2026, the average diesel price in the European Union was 20 percent higher than a year earlier. The largest increases were recorded in Romania and the Netherlands, both at 31 percent, followed by Germany at 27 percent, France at 24 percent and Greece at 22 percent.

croatia remains below the eu average

With a 14 percent increase, Croatia remained six percent below the EU average. A slightly milder increase was recorded in Slovenia at 13 percent, while Hungary, with a rise of only one percent, is clearly at the bottom of the observed group of countries.The difference is even more pronounced for petrol specifically. Its price across the rest of the European Union rose by an average of 15 percent over the year, almost twice as much as in Croatia.

The largest increase was recorded in Lithuania at 25 percent, followed by Romania at 23 percent, Germany at 22 percent and the Netherlands at 21 percent. In France and Poland, petrol rose by 16 percent, and in Austria by 15 percent. Croatia and neighbouring Italy, both with an eight percent increase, are at the bottom of the presented ranking. In Slovenia, petrol rose by nine percent, and in Greece by 13 percent.

The annual growth data comes at a time when Croatian drivers are being hit by yet another new price increase. The government adopted decrees at a telephone session under which a litre of petrol costs 1.66 euros as of Tuesday, three cents more than before. Diesel rose by six cents to 1.86 euros per litre, and blue diesel by five cents to 1.32 euros. Liquefied petroleum gas also rose in price. LPG for tanks now costs 1.27 euros per kilogram, three cents more, while the price of gas in bottles rose by four cents to 1.85 euros per kilogram.

The government has retained reduced excise duties and limited traders’ margins. According to its calculation, without these measures petrol would cost 1.81 euros and diesel 2.07 euros per litre. The new prices are valid for seven days.

there will be no shortages, but prices will go up

Energy expert Jasminko Umićević assessed that Croatia is not facing a fuel shortage, but warns that high prices could persist. The problem is particularly pronounced on the diesel market, whose price has remained high even after the fall in the price of crude oil. Over the past twenty years or so, Europe has reduced its refining capacity by approximately 30 percent, even though it consumes more diesel than across the pond in America. After the interruption of imports from Russia, it has relied more on Arab countries, and disruptions related to the Strait of Hormuz have further reduced supply.

Croatia is in a more favourable position thanks to the Rijeka refinery. Although it isn’t yet operating at full capacity because testing is ongoing, domestic production reduces dependence on imports and the risk of shortages.

World.title: Croatian Economy Grows 1.8% in Second Quarter of 2026
World.content:
August the 27th, 2026 – The Croatian economy will likely see growth of 1.8% in the second quarter of 2026, pointing to an economic slowdown.

The movement of the CEIZ index suggests that the Croatian economy will grow by 1.8 percent in the second quarter of 2026 compared to the same period last year, according to analysts at the Zagreb Economic Institute (EIZ). Poslovni reports that the CEIZ index fell by 1.24 index points back in June compared to the same month last year, while its value decreased by 0.15 index points compared to May.

In June this year, among the indicators tracking economic activity, tourism actually underperformed the most, with the number of tourist arrivals lower than in May. On the other hand, industrial production and retail trade turnover rose, and the state collected more VAT revenue. The number of tourist arrivals was also the only component of the CEIZ index that recorded a decline in June compared to the same month last year.

“The described movement of the index suggests that economic activity in the second quarter of 2026 is slightly slowing compared to the previous quarter. Despite this, we estimate that the Croatian economy will grow by 1.8 percent year-on-year in the second quarter, with a positive quarter-on-quarter rate of change,” the EIZ analysts state.

The Institute emphasised that the estimate based on the CEIZ index is not a precise forecast of GDP growth, but rather serves as a kind of ‘compass’ for monitoring current economic activity. The Croatian economy is therefore still growing, but at a somewhat slower pace than at the beginning of the year. CEIZ data so far doesn’t point to a turnaround, but rather to a gradual slowdown in economic activity.

World.title: Billionaires Gather on 200 Million Euro Yacht Near Mljet
World.content:
August the 26th, 2026 – Multiple billionaires have come together on a 200 million euro yacht near the southern Croatian island of Mljet. Jeff Bezos, and Jan Koum are among them.

Poslovni reports that this impressive vessel can accommodate 16 guests along with 32 crew members, and the yacht’s price is nearly 200 million euros. Mljet is set to be hosting a meeting of two of the world’s biggest technology billionaires, Jan Koum and Jeff Bezos, over the next few days. They met on Koum’s yacht worth nearly 200 million dollars.

Jan Koum, co-founder of WhatsApp whose wealth is estimated at 17 billion dollars, anchored his superyacht Moonrise near Mljet, and the same day Jeff Bezos, owner of Amazon, arrived in the company of American media mogul Barry Diller. Koum arrived on the Moonrise by helicopter on Monday, and Bezos visited him in the late afternoon hours. The three billionaires, Koum, Bezos and Diller, thus found themselves on the same vessel in the middle of the Adriatic Sea.

Koum is no stranger to the Croatian coast; he has holidayed in our beautiful country before. His superyacht Moonrise was photographed between the islands of Lopud and Šipan back in 2021 and 2024, and it was recorded that on one occasion he arrived for a summer holiday in Croatia with as many as three vessels: in addition to Moonrise he was accompanied by the 74-metre yacht Mogambo and the 55-metre Power Play, which served him as a helipad. The Amazon owner regularly summers on the Mediterranean on his superyacht Koru, where he cruised the Adriatic in the summers of 2023 and 2025, with recorded stays on Hvar, Mljet, Korčula, and a visit to the Šibenik archipelago.

The yacht Moonrise isn’t just an ordinary vessel. It’s a 100-metre superyacht from the Dutch shipyard Feadship, built in 2020. The sophisticated exterior design is by De Voogt, while the interior is the work of French designer Rémi Tessier. The vessel can accommodate 16 guests along with 32 crew members, and the yacht’s price is nearly 200 million euros.

World.title: Pula Receives 12 Electric Buses Worth 6.8 Million Euros
World.content:
August the 26th, 2026 – Pula has received 12 electric buses worth a total of 6.8 million euros with an aim of increasing passenger comfort and being more environmentally friendly.

Pulapromet has put another six new electric buses into service, thereby completing the project of acquiring a total of 12 electric vehicles for Pula’s public transport. Index reports that the project was fully financed with funds from the National Recovery and Resilience Plan, and the total value of the purchased buses amounts to 6,763,900 euros. For the project, Pulapromet had been allocated 6,994,998 euros, but after the public procurement procedure the total value was somewhat lower.

Specifically speaking, Pulapromet acquired six MAN and six Iveco electric buses. Director Tomislav Josipović said that this is an important step in modernising the vehicle fleet and raising the quality of public transport.

“By putting these new six electric buses into service today, we are completing the project through which Pulapromet has received a total of 12 new electric vehicles,” said Josipović, adding that almost 6.8 million euros of investment has been directed into the development of public transport without any financial burden on Pulapromet. The new buses should reduce emissions of harmful gases and noise while increasing energy efficiency and passenger comfort.

an increase in public transport use in pula

Pula Mayor Peđa Grbin said that the project does not stop at the acquisition of buses. He announced the installation of solar panels on the canopy at the depot (Remiza), for which the City is waiting for the opening of appropriate co-financing tenders. “The goal is for these electric buses to run on electricity that will be produced here, in Pula, from the most ecological possible source, which is solar energy,” said Grbin. He added that since the beginning of the year the use of public city transport has increased by almost 10 percent. According to him, this has also been contributed to by the City of Pula’s decisions on free transport for pupils, students and pensioners.

Istria County Prefect Boris Miletić thanked the City of Pula, Pulapromet, the surrounding municipalities and the Ministry of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure for implementing the project. He emphasised that electric buses, especially if powered by energy from solar sources, can contribute to reducing the impact of traffic on the environment. Miletić also said that Pulapromet first secured the infrastructure and charging stations, and then acquired the vehicles. He assessed that higher-quality public transport could further increase the number of passengers.

World.title: Istria Showcased in Front of Millions of German Viewers
World.content:
August the 26th, 2026 – Gorgeous Istria has been showcased in front of millions of German viewers, shining the spotlight on Croatia’s largest peninsula.

Morski reports that one of the most successful German travel programmes, “Wunderschön”, devoted a full 90 minutes of airtime to Istria, presenting the diversity of the peninsula to a million-strong audience in the German-speaking world – from Kamenjak, Pula and the Brijuni Islands, via Učka, Buzet and Pazin, to Poreč and Rovinj.

The project was realised in cooperation between the Tourist Board of Istria County and its long-standing PR partner ART Redaktionsteam from Salzburg. Viewers are guided through Istria by well-known German television presenter Stephanie Müller-Spirra, under the direction of award-winning journalist and author Stephan Heise. Alongside numerous local protagonists, the programme also features Marko Purišić – Baby Lasagna, Rade Šerbedžija and extreme alpinist Ines Papert. Istria is presented to the audience through a blend of natural and cultural attractions, active holidays, local stories and top-class food and local wine.

The first broadcast of the report reaches around two million viewers, while through further screenings in Germany, Austria and Switzerland the total viewership is expected to exceed five million, making the project one of the most significant television promotions of Istria on its most important outbound market.

World.title: Iraqi army reaffirms putting all weapons under state control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi military reaffirmed on Thursday its commitment to implementing the government’s goal of putting all weapons under state control, stating that it is an irreversible sovereign matter.

The spokesperson for the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, Sabah al-Numan, stated that the government remains dedicated to regulating firearms and guaranteeing that they are under the control of the state and its official security agencies.

Al-Numan stated that a specialist committee had been created and that discussions were underway on how to control weapons in a way that preserves them, adding that the issue was a fundamental demand.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is spearheading the government’s proposal to bring all weaponry under strict state control to strengthen national sovereignty, enforce the rule of law, and keep the country out of regional wars.

The effort aims to abolish autonomous armed power by September 30, 2026, when the military mission of the US-led international coalition comes to an end.

Armed factions such as Asaib Ahl al-Haq and Kataib al-Imam Ali have started to sever their autonomous ties to fully integrate into official governmental institutions.

The Iraqi Interior Ministry extended the national weapons registration procedure to the end of 2026, while continuing to purchase medium-range firearms from individuals.

Security personnel are actively targeting unauthorized organizations, carrying out raids and seizing illegal weapons.

Iraqi policymakers are considering a compromise solution to avoid deadly riots. Iran-aligned militias may keep their weapons under the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), a state-recognized paramilitary organization, instead of handing them over directly to official authorities.

Factions including Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada refuse to disarm as long as any foreign military presence continues in the country.

While September 30 marks the departure of foreign forces, security officials emphasize that the date represents the start of a gradual, long-term weapon control process, not an absolute deadline for ultimate disarmament.

World.title: Iraq, Qatar’s UCC discuss oil pipeline projects to bypass Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair met on Tuesday with officials from Qatar’s UCC Holding in Baghdad to discuss critical oil pipeline projects that aim to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The discussions addressed establishing technical frameworks, project schedules, and contractual structures for the Basra-Haditha-Fishkhabur pipeline to Turkey and the Haditha-Baniyas pipeline to Syria, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Oil Ministry.

Iraq is prioritizing this oil pipeline network to build alternate export routes to the Mediterranean to minimize its longstanding vulnerability and reliance on maritime shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Khudair underlined the importance of accelerating formal contractual procedures. He requested weekly meetings between Iraqi authorities and the consortium to finalize the pipeline paths and economic models.

Qatar-based UCC Holding is leading the consortium that includes Chevron, TI Capital, and TotalEnergies to carry out the project.

The project is a network of pipelines that will be extended to the Turkish port of Ceyhan and the Syrian port of Baniyas, providing two additional outlets to enhance export flexibility.

The pipeline network will provide the country with additional export outlets on the Mediterranean, significantly reducing the risks of maritime shipping via the Strait of Hormuz.

Khudair said earlier that a country like Iraq, with its vast oil and gas reserves, cannot continue to rely on a single outlet, the Strait of Hormuz.

The Basra-Haditha pipeline project is an Iraqi venture estimated at $4.6 billion aiming to transport crude oil from the southern Iraqi province of Basra to Haditha in the western Iraqi province of Anbar.

The pipeline’s capacity is projected to be approximately 2.25 million barrels per day using 56-inch diameter pipes. This design aims to enhance domestic transportation and establish connections to future export facilities.

Reaching Haditha opens up three distinct offshore export routes: the Turkish port of Ceyhan, the Syrian port of Baniyas, and Jordan’s port of Aqaba.

Iraq’s planned oil pipeline network represents a proactive strategy to reduce dependency on Gulf marine routes, which face disruptions.

The Basra-Fishkhabur pipeline project is one of Iraq’s largest strategic energy initiatives, connecting southern oil reserves to the Turkish border.

World.title: Iraq, Shell discuss increasing gas output from Basra’s oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Oil Ministry and Shell discussed on Wednesday strategic plans to increase gas production from oil fields in the southern province of Basra.

Deputy Oil Minister for Extraction Affairs Naseer Aziz and Shell’s Managing Director for Iraq and the UAE Fakher Bader led the discussions, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The discussions focused on increasing the total production capacity of the Basra Gas Company (BGC), a joint venture between Iraq’s South Gas Company (SGC), Shell, and Mitsubishi, and speeding up the recovery of associated gas from southern oil fields.

To maximize state earnings, both parties reviewed strategies to increase naphtha production and exports.

The direct recovery of associated gas supports Iraq’s environmental goal to significantly reduce gas flaring at oil fields.

The initiative seeks to guarantee a reliable and stable fuel supply for domestic industries and power plants, thereby alleviating electricity shortages.

Amid regional transit issues impacting regular crude lines, enhancing hydrocarbon value through domestic gas networks provides Baghdad with critical financial stability.

World.title: Barcola move from PSG to Liverpool ‘on track’: source
World.content:
Paris – Transfer talks between Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain over an Anfield move for Bradley Barcola are “on the right track”, a source close to the negotiations said on Thursday.

The France winger has already agreed personal terms with Liverpool, according to several media reports.

The two clubs have reportedly agreed a transfer fee which could rise to 140 million euros (£120 million, $163 million).

That would make Barcola Liverpool’s second-most expensive signing, after Alexander Isak, and would be the most money ever paid for a Ligue 1 player.

Barcola is yet to play for PSG this season amid the transfer speculation.

Liverpool have been looking to strengthen in wide areas since the departure of club great Mohamed Salah at the end of last term.

They have already signed Spain winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna in the current transfer window.

Barcola would be a statement signing for new Reds manager Andoni Iraola.

The 23-year-old scored three goals for France during their run to the semi-finals at the recent World Cup.

He was not always first-choice at PSG, with Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue providing stiff competition for places.

But Barcola still played a key part in the capital giants winning back-to-back Champions League titles.

He has also won three Ligue 1 titles and two French Cups with PSG since joining from Lyon in 2023, scoring 39 goals in 152 appearances.

Liverpool are bidding to bounce back from a disappointing campaign last season, when their Premier League title defence ended in a fifth-placed finish, leading to the sacking of boss Arne Slot.

They rescued a 2-2 draw at Newcastle in their opening game of the season last weekend.

Luis Enrique’s PSG have been busy in the transfer market, selling Goncalo Ramos, Randal Kolo Muani and Lee Kang-in, while bringing in Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Lucas Digne.

World.title: Swallowed by silt: Survivors recount Nepal flood horror
World.content:
Bidur – Survivors from Nepal’s flood-ravaged districts, some on stretchers, others gently supported by the shoulders, were airlifted to safety on Thursday as the constant roar of helicopters echoed across the devastated town of Bidur.

A few walked alone, their faces frozen in shock, as helicopters landed every few minutes on a football field inside the town’s military cantonment, whipping up clouds of dust.

Among the survivors was customs agent Omkar Joshi, who spent the previous night stranded on a hilltop in the border town of Timure before being rescued.

“Everything is finished,” Joshi, 35, told AFP, his voice breaking with emotion.

The town he fled had all but vanished beneath a torrent of water, mud and debris.

“Ninety percent” of its people were dead, he said, swallowed by silt.

“It is a giant graveyard. All that is left are sand and pebbles, soaked red by human blood.”

He said hundreds of people survived only by scrambling up nearby slopes as floodwaters roared through the valley below.

“It rained all night, but we stayed put till the choppers came for us,” he added.

On Wednesday, a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through villages and towns along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Nepali police have recovered 270 bodies, but search operations continue.

Many of the missing are foreign tourists caught in the disaster, which according to the US Geological Survey was caused by a glacial collapse that resulted in an overwhelming flow of icy debris.

– Buried alive –

In Bidur, scores of anxious relatives peered through the barbed wire separating the football ground from the road, hoping to see the familiar face of a loved one.

Sita BK was searching for her younger brother Ramchandra, a schoolteacher in Timure.

“I spoke to him in the morning just before I heard the news,” said the 37-year-old. “But ever since, his phone is switched off.”

She said she had no choice but to wait.

“They (officials) said their first priority is to rescue people who are contactable,” she said. “But my brother is not.”

Nearby, Anisha Nepali sat quietly in a corner, tears running down her cheeks.

The 24-year-old had rushed back from Kathmandu on Wednesday after hearing about the disaster, but has received no news of her missing mother and younger brother.

“I have given their names, but am yet to hear anything,” she said.

Two young girls climbed out of a helicopter, still in their bright green school uniforms. A rescuer gently caressed their heads and offered them biscuits and water, before leading them away to safety.

Farther downstream, the devastation was etched into the shattered landscape of Devighat.

Residents said only one of roughly 150 houses along the banks of the Trishuli River remained intact: a four-storey old-age care home.

But rescuers said up to seven elderly residents were buried when a landslide crashed into the home as they tried to flee.

Images shared by a rescuer showed one of the victims trapped beneath an uprooted tree.

Sabir Miyan, a resident of the town, said warnings that floodwaters were racing down from the mountains had helped save lives.

“Many of us could save our lives but everything else is gone,” he said. “It is all ruins now.”

World.title: Search for 1,300 missing after deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
World.content:
Bidur – Rescue teams scoured devastated zones Thursday for more than 1,300 people missing a day after flash floods and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border killed at least 273, sweeping away entire villages.

Homes were engulfed and vehicles tossed around by the tsunami-like rumble of water and mud that struck villages and towns on Wednesday morning on the path of two rivers, Bhote Koshi and Trishuli.

Many of the missing are foreign tourists, including scores of Hindu pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred snow-capped Mount Kailash.

According to the US Geological Survey, the disaster was caused by a glacial collapse that sent forth an overwhelming flow of icy debris.

Emergency teams were racing to evacuate survivors from affected zones, fearing new flash floods.

Nepali soldiers used sniffer dogs to search for bodies buried under thick grey sludge.

“Everything is finished,” Omkar Joshi, 35, a Nepali customs agent rescued from a hilltop in the border town of Timure, told AFP.

“It is a giant graveyard. All that is left are sand and pebbles, soaked red by human blood.”

Nepali police said they had recovered 270 bodies.

Another 823 people, including 517 foreign tourists, were out of contact in the country. Beijing says 100 Chinese citizens are missing in Nepal.

In China, state media said the “mudslide disaster” at the Gyirong Port in Tibet killed three people, while 558 people, including 260 foreigners, are missing.

Chinese Premier Li Qiang visited the area on Thursday, state media said, to oversee “emergency rescue and relief work, and to visit rescue workers and affected people”.

– ‘Inland tsunami’ –

In Nepal, rescuers waded through mud and sludge to look for survivors after floodwaters buried the lower floors of multi-storey buildings.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who urged the Himalyan nation to “stand together” hours after the disaster, visited some of the hardest-hit areas on Thursday.

Shah told local authorities to “provide immediate relief to displaced families” and to open blocked roads, his office said in a statement.

The foreigners out of contact included Indians and others from Australia, Britain, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Portugal, South Africa, South Korea and the United States, Nepal’s tourism board said.

The sudden rush of mud and debris was “like an inland tsunami”, travelling nearly 170 kilometres (100 miles) south into Nepal, said environmental historian Ruth Gamble, of Australia’s La Trobe University.

Rasuwa, in the north of Nepal, was the first district to be affected, but deaths have been reported as far south as Chitwan in the south, on the border with India.

Buddhist spiritual leader the Dalai Lama, who lives in exile in India, said he would “pray for all those who have lost their lives”.

Chinese government officials in Tibet mobilised nearly 800 emergency workers, as well as sniffer dogs and speed boats to help the rescue efforts, official news agency Xinhua said.

Promises of aid and assistance came in soon after reports of the scale of the disaster.

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies said it was dispatching emergency supplies including blankets, first aid kits, stretchers and body bags.

– Glacial collapse –

The US Geological Survey said the flood was sparked by a glacial collapse, that caused seismic activity and the “catastrophic” downstream impacts in Nepal and Tibet.

“This event was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake,” it said, but added that the seismic recordings were analysed and found instead to be a “glacial collapse and debris flow”.

Climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of glacial lake floods and glacial collapses.

Fears of potential further floods remain, with water trapped by the immense piles of debris blocking the valley.

“With a blockage still lodged upstream on the Nepal-China border river, authorities warn a second flood may occur,” said Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.

Li Qipu, a member of China’s paramilitary People’s Armed Police, cited “the instability of a reservoir lake upstream” and “the narrow mountain road” as elements complicating rescue efforts.

Scores of Hindu devotees from across the world are among the hundreds missing on the border, Indian spiritual leader Sadhguru said Thursday.

They had been returning from a holy pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, on the Chinese side of the frontier, when they were caught in the floods at an immigration post.

“The entire group was there in the building,” Sadhguru said in a video message to his millions of followers, weeping as he spoke from Tibet, with the anguished wails of other pilgrims heard in the background.

“This is a terrible and extraordinary event.”

World.title: Iraq’s central bank denies issuing banknotes with three zeros removed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) officially denied reports that it has issued new banknotes with three zeros deleted.

The CBI said in a statement that allegations of producing new currency denominations are unfounded and have no official source.

Any future plans to redenominate the currency or eliminate zeros must go through extensive legal, regulatory, and technical processes, according to the statement.

The CBI urged citizens and media outlets to rely solely on official channels to avoid public misunderstanding and market speculation.

Lawmakers and government officials have lately discussed ideas to remove three zeros from the Iraqi dinar to return stockpiled currency to the legitimate banking system and combat corruption.

According to Jamal Kocher, a Kurdish member of the Iraqi parliament’s finance committee, Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has asked for the removal of zeros from invoices.

Kocher told The New Region that if the plan is implemented, 1,000 Iraqi dinars would be converted to one dinar, while 25,000 dinars would be equivalent to 25 dinars.

Earlier in August, Communications Minister Mustafa Sanad acknowledged the plan to eliminate the zeros and modify the currency.

Despite public discussion and declarations, the CBI has yet to publish a clear timeframe or complete a plan for any currency reform.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate against Iraqi dinar continues to fall
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar continued to decline on Wednesday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate dropped in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,539.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,545 Iraqi dinars and 1,535 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate declined, fluctuating between 1,539.5 and 1,539 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

âWe have understood how much affection you (Devendra Fadnavis) have for the Marathi language and for our state.

You go to Gujarat, you go to Punjab, you go to the South. Everywhere there is an attachment to oneâs own language.â

The remarks come after the Maharashtra government gave auto-rickshaw, taxi and cab drivers an additional year to learn functional Marathi.





Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis announced the extension on Thursday after representatives of driversâ organisations sought more time, citing the varied ages and educational backgrounds of those working in the sector.

"Today, people from the auto drivers' and rickshaw drivers' organisations met with me. They first expressed their support for the idea that functional Marathi should be learned by those working in Mumbai.

They all want to learn it, but along with that, they also said that people of various ages are in this profession, and many have dropped out of studies a long time ago," Fadnavis said.

The Maharashtra government had made practical knowledge of Marathi mandatory for commercial passenger vehicle drivers, including auto-rickshaw, taxi and app-based cab drivers, from August 12.

The requirement was announced by Maharashtra Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik and formalised through the Maharashtra Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Rules, 2026, which amended the existing 1989 rules to include language requirements.

Under the amended rules, drivers unable to demonstrate a working knowledge of Marathi could face suspension of their driving licence authorisation for three months. Repeat violations could result in permanent cancellation of their permits.

Fadnavis said the government had considered the difficulties faced by drivers from different age groups and educational backgrounds while retaining the requirement that those working in Mumbai have a basic working knowledge of Marathi.

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Thursday criticised the Centre over the functioning of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), alleging that the system treats ordinary borrowers differently from large corporate borrowers.Calling the NCLT the âLeader-Company Loot Tribunalâ, Rahul contrasted the treatment of farmers, salaried workers and students with that of what he described as a select group of wealthy businesspersons."If a farmer doesnât pay 50 thousand, his land gets auctioned off. However, he said the claims of lenders who had objected to his repayment plan amounted to Rs 3,992 crore. Of this, Rs 620 crore had already been settled, leaving Rs 3,372 crore, he said.

World.title: PM Modi to meet Putin on SCO summit sidelines during Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan visit
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uzbekistan and the Kyrgyz Republic from August 29 to September 1, the ministry of external affairs said on Thursday.During his four-day visit, PM Modi will undertake a bilateral visit to Tashkent and participate in the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit in Bishkek.PM Modi will also hold bilateral meetings with SCO leaders on the sidelines of the summit. According to news agency PTI, Putin will also be among the leaders with whom PM Modi will hold bilateral meetings on the margins of the summit.PM Modi is also expected to visit the Shastri Memorial in Tashkent and the Mahatma Gandhi Centre at the Tashkent State University of Oriental Studies.This will be PM Modi's fourth visit and his second bilateral visit to Uzbekistan, according to MEA Secretary (West) Sibi George.Addressing a special briefing on the Prime Minister's visit, MEA Secretary (West) said India and Uzbekistan have maintained "extensive and fruitful engagements" over the years in both bilateral and multilateral formats.Highlighting the depth of economic ties, the MEA Secretary said India is among Uzbekistan's top 10 trading partners, with bilateral trade and investments together close to USD 1 billion."We have wide-ranging cooperation in the fields of critical minerals, pharma, education, information technology, and the health sector," he said.The summit coincides with the SCO's 25th anniversary of its founding. After serving as an observer since 2005, India became a full member of the organisation in 2017.From August 31 to September 1, the Prime Minister will visit Bishkek, George stated.According to the MEA, the organisation's main goal was to combat the three "evils" of terrorism, separatism and extremism, which continue to present challenges.

World.title: In a 1st, TN CM Vijay ditches his chair, sits with ministers in assembly
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

C Joseph Vijay broke with a long-standing assembly convention on Thursday when he left his designated chair and took a seat alongside ministers in the front row during the afternoon session.

It was unusual for a chief minister to occupy a seat meant for ministers, news agency PTI reported citing a source.

Vijay, who normally sits in a separate chair positioned close to Speaker J C D Prabhakar, moved across the front row and sat between ministers K A Sengottaiyan, who is also the leader of the House, and Aadhav Arjuna.

Members of the House occasionally change seats briefly to interact with colleagues. However, Vijay's move was notable because he shifted from his official chair and remained seated among the ministers.

World.content:
A barrier lake near the China-Nepal border may breach in three days as flash floods and mudslides have killed at least 273 people and left over 1,300 missing.

India is tracing 288 nationals unaccounted for after Nepal floods, while around 200 Indians in Tibet have sought help. India has also sent a second relief consignment to Nepal.

Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge wrote to PM Modi seeking a 25-year freeze on Lok Sabha seat strength and an all-party meeting before any delimitation exercise.

YouTuber Chhavi Varshney and her mother died after their SUV crashed into a truck near Ujjain. Three others were seriously injured, with police investigating the accident.

A 42-year-old woman in Pinjore named her husband as her killer in a dying message after her throat was slit. Police arrested her husband within two hours.

World.title: 'Nation is confused': Congress alleges 'plan to change narrative' on China role in Op Sindoor
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

leader Jairam Ramesh on Thursday questioned what he described as conflicting statements by senior military officials on the extent of cooperation between Pakistan and China during

.

Sharing video clips on X, Ramesh said Deputy Chief of Army Staff Lt Gen Rahul Singh had, on July 4, 2025, highlighted what he called the âvery disturbingly deep natureâ of the Pakistan-China partnership during the military operation.

The Congress leader contrasted those remarks with comments made by former Chief of Defence Staff Gen. Anil Chauhan on August 25, 2026, saying Chauhan's account appeared to be âsimply oppositeâ to that of Lt.

Gen. Singh.

âOn July 4 2025, the Deputy Chief of Army Staff Lt. Gen Rahul Singh had revealed the very disturbingly deep nature of the Pakistan-China jugalbandi during Operation Sindoor. On Aug 25, 2026, the former Chief of Defence Staff Gen. Anil Chauhan made his own revelations on this jugalbandi - which are simply opposite to what Lt. Gen Singh had said. The nation is confused," said Ramesh on X.

The Congress leader questioned whether the differing accounts reflected a broader effort to shape the public narrative around India's relations with China.





âWhat is going on here? Is there some deeper plan to change the narrative?â he asked.

He also linked the issue to the Centre's broader China policy, alleging that there had been a âcalibrated capitulation to Chinaâ and citing what he described as the Prime Minister's âinfamous clean chit to China on June 2020â as well as India's record trade deficits with China.

World.title: Pregnant woman treated for spinal tuberculosis through surgery
World.content:
The surgeons at Meenakshi Super Speciality Hospital (MSSH) treated a 28-year-old pregnant woman for spinal tuberculosis through a challenging spinal surgery performed at her 28th week of pregnancy, positioning her prone throughout the procedure.

Speaking to media persons, the doctors said the surgical team used specialised abdominal and fetal shielding techniques to ensure the safety of both the mother and the fetus. Meticulous measures were taken to minimise foetal radiation exposure during intraoperative C-arm imaging. The woman recovered well and recently delivered a healthy baby after her full term of pregnancy, they said.

The patient had experienced neck pain for nearly a year. She was admitted to the hospital within days of developing progressive sensory loss, difficulty in walking and loss of sensation below the chest.

An MRI scan revealed spondylodiscitis, an infection involving spinal bones and disc between them at T1–T2 level; severe gibbus deformity, a hump-like deformity of the spine, and compressive myelopathy, a dysfunction of the spinal cord caused by pressure on it.

All these symptoms raised clinical suspicion of spinal tuberculosis — also known as Pott’s spine. The progressive neurological deficit and spinal instability necessitated immediate surgical intervention.

The surgical team performed T1-T2 decompressive laminectomy to relieve pressure on the spinal cord, along with biopsy and removal of infected tissue from the affected spinal segment. This was followed by C3-T4 spinal fusion using metal implants and the patient’s own bone graft to stabilise the spine.

The tissue and vertebral fragments obtained during surgery were sent for histopathological evaluation. The examination revealed acute inflammation along with a small focus of epithelioid granuloma, an immune response commonly associated with tuberculosis.

The surgical procedures were led by doctors K. Selvamuthukumaran, K. Senthil Kumar and K.M. Kaveeze.

World.title: 13 arrested for murder of Congress leader and his son in West Bengal
World.content:
TMC activist Jubbar Sheikh, currently in jail, was allegedly responsible for the plot; his wife, Fatima Bibi, has also been arrested

Krishnanagar police have arrested 13 people in connection with the murder of Congress leader Anisur Rahman and his son Abu Sufiyan at Nakasipara in the Nadia district of West Bengal on August 15, officials said on Thursday (August 27, 2026).

Krishnanagar SP, Atul V, stated, “A total of 13 people, including suspects from Karnataka and Odisha, have been arrested in the Nakasipara double murder and vehicles used in the crime have been seized.”

The two were killed by miscreants on a motorcycle who fired upon their vehicle at the Nakasipara railway gate. After several rounds were fired at the vehicle, the two were dragged out and hacked to death.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said activists of the Trinamool Congress (TMC) were behind the murder. A criminal named Jubbar Sheikh allegedly plotted the murders from jail. His wife, Fatima Bibi — a TMC member and local panchayat head — was arrested the next day along with her two associates, Ali Mandal and Mithun Sheikh.

The SP added, “Ten more people were arrested later. Following interrogations of the suspects, a huge cache of arms and ammunition used in committing the crime was recovered today.”

According to the officials, 13 weapons and 100 rounds of ammunition were seized from the accused.

World.title: Manickam Tagore demands release of ₹5,109 crore in Samagra Shiksha funds for Tamil Nadu
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Congress Committee president K. Manickam Tagore has accused the BJP-led Union government of withholding ₹5,109 crore in education funds due to Tamil Nadu under the Samagra Shiksha scheme over the past three years.

In a statement, Mr. Tagore said the Union government had withheld ₹1,788 crore in 2024-25, ₹1,496 crore in 2025-26 and ₹1,825 crore in the current financial year, citing figures from the Tamil Nadu School Education Department’s policy note.

He alleged that the Centre had released only ₹714 crore towards the Right to Education (RTE) scheme despite a Supreme Court order, while continuing to withhold other school education funds. The Tamil Nadu government had continued to run its schools despite the lack of central assistance, allocating ₹2,014 crore from its own funds over the past two years and ₹647 crore in the current year, he said.

He alleged that the withholding of funds was affecting initiatives aimed at improving learning outcomes among government school students, teacher training and school infrastructure. The Congress MP also accused the Centre of using the issue to pressure Tamil Nadu over its opposition to the three-language policy and its refusal to implement the PM-SHRI scheme and the National Education Policy (NEP).

Calling the move an “assault on federalism”, Mr. Tagore said he had written to Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi seeking the immediate release of the ₹5,109 crore due to Tamil Nadu without any conditions.

World.title: Water levels subside in Bihar rivers, reducing flood risks a day after Nepal tragedy
World.content:
A day after a flash flood killed hundreds in Nepal and threatened to overflow into neighboring Bihar, the risk of flooding in the Gandak, Ganga, and other tributary rivers subsided significantly on Thursday. However, debris and cattle carcasses were seen in the Gandak, which is called the Narayani river on the Nepal side of the border.

Follow the updates of the Nepal flash floods on August 27, 2026.

Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, accompanied by top government officials, conducted an aerial survey of the Valmikingar barrage areas of West Champaran district along the Indo-Nepal border, which had faced an imminent threat till Thursday (August 27, 2026) afternoon.

“It is God’s grace that we are safe. The way disaster had struck Nepal is a matter of concern. The Prime Minister and Union Home Minister were continuously keeping a close watch on Bihar,” Mr. Choudhary told journalists. “The situation is gradually becoming normal… The discharge at the barrage was around 1 lakh cusecs today. The danger is subsiding now,” he added.

Water flow decreasing

Fearing a flash flood in the Gandak, all 36 gates of the Valmikinagar barrage had been opened on Wednesday (August 26, 2026). By nightfall, the flow of water there had shot up by 20,000 cusecs, prompting senior Water Resources Department (WRD) engineers and district officials to prepare for a further deterioration of the situation. The barrage also started witnessing three-metre-high waves, and the water gush peaked at 1.5 lakh cusecs on Thursday afternoon. It then “started decreasing”, one of the senior engineers confirmed.

The rise in water discharge at the barrage was expected to increase to 2.5 lakh cusecs. One cusec, or cubic feet per second, amounts to 28.32 litres of water flowing past any particular point within one second.

In the border areas of northern Bihar, residents stayed glued to their mobile phones on Wednesday night, awaiting any updates on the possible flood threat in their areas. WRD engineers and district officials also kept vigil at rivers and embankments, alerting people through microphones, and only heaved a sigh of relief on Thursday when the incoming gush of flood waters decreased continuously.

‘Continous vigil’

Water levels also receded in the Ganga river at some places in Patna on Thursday (August 27), providing relief to residents of Patna, Vaishali, Bhagalpur, and Begusarai districts, which have also been reeling from floods for the last few days. “However, the State WRD department has been keeping continuous vigil on the situation and is all alert in view of the flood security,” a government statement said on Thursday.

The CM’s aerial survey, conducted along with Deputy CM Vijay Kumar Choudhary, covered the Valmikinagar, Bagaha and Bettiah areas of West Champaran. It was aimed at assessing the flood situation and reviewing the administration’s preparations for rescue and relief operations.

“Ensuring the safety of the people and providing them every possible relief and assistance are the topmost priority of the State government,” he said, directing officials to take all necessary measures in this regard.

‘Stay alert and safe’

The Leader of Opposition in the State Assembly, Tejashwi Yadav, urged people in high-risk areas to remain “alert and safe”, just before he set off to Delhi with family members. Speaking at the Patna airport, Mr. Yadav said, “It was traumatic to watch visuals of what happened in Nepal on Wednesday so I would urge people living in bordering areas to stay alert and safe.” His parents, the former CMs Lalu Prasad Yadav and Rabri Devi were also seen leaving for Delhi.

Of the State’s 38 districts, the Disaster Management Department has declared 29 districts — 21 in north Bihar and eight in south Bihar — as flood prone. “Vagaries of weather due to several environmental factors have put planners at a crossroad because Bihar is often witnessing flood-like situations in one part at the same time as other areas go through drought-like situation,” said a statement issued by experts at the G.P. Sinha Memorial lecture series on ‘Budhi Gandak-Bagmati and other river inter-linking: Creating a dynamic flood management system’.

World.title: 400 missing mobile phones recovered from various States, handed over to owners
World.content:
The Triplicane police have recovered 400 mobile phones reported missing from various police stations’ limits in the Triplicane police district. The phones, which were traced to different States across India, were handed over to their rightful owners on Thursday.

Complaints regarding missing mobile phones were received at police stations under the Triplicane police district and entered in the Community Service Register. The Cyber Crime Wing and special teams of the Triplicane police subsequently launched an investigation to trace the devices.

As part of the investigation, police used the Central Equipment Identity Register (CEIR) portal to track the International Mobile Equipment Identity (IMEI) numbers of the missing and stolen phones. Continued monitoring revealed that several of the devices were being used in Tamil Nadu and other States.

Police teams then traced the persons using the phones and conducted inquiries, following which the missing devices were recovered. A total of 400 mobile phones were recovered and the ownership details were verified before they were returned.

At the office of the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Triplicane district, in Chintadripet. Deputy Commissioner Jayachandran handed over the recovered mobile phones to their respective owners.

The police advised the public to lodge a complaint at the nearest police station and register the device on the CEIR portal immediately if a mobile phone is lost or stolen.

World.title: Four farmers attacked by wild boar in Ramanathapuram; admitted to hospital
World.content:
In a shocking incident, four farmers on their way to work were attacked by a wild boar at Thimmanathapuram near Perunazhi in Ramanathapuram district on Thursday.

According to information reaching the district headquarters, the four farmers, Selvam (45), Muthalagar (35), Mariswaran (31) and Sasivarnam (35), all from the same hamlet, were walking along the road towards a nearby field.

Suddenly, a wild boar that emerged from the bushes attacked Selvam. When the others attempted to chase away the animal, they too suffered injuries.

On information, local residents alerted the ambulance service and the four were admitted to the Aruppukottai Government Hospital for treatment.

The family members appealed to the government to provide treatment to the injured and ensure their safety. The animals should either be captured and driven back into the forest or appropriate steps taken to prevent such attacks, they pleaded.

World.title: Five-day Lok Samvardhan Parv-2026 to be held in Bengaluru from September 26
World.content:
A five-day ‘Lok Samvardhan Parv-2026’, aimed at promoting cultural activities and empowerment of minority communities, will be held at Palace Grounds in Bengaluru from September 26, Minister for Housing, Wakf and Minority Welfare U.T. Khader said on Thursday.

Addressing presspersons, the Minister said the event is being organised in collaboration with the Union Ministry of Minority Affairs. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, and Union Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju will inaugurate the event on the morning of September 26. Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara and Ministers Priyank Kharge, K.J. George, Zameer Ahmed Khan and Rizwan Arshad are among those expected to attend.

180 stalls to showcase crafts

The event will provide a platform to showcase cultural arts, handicrafts, and other products made by minority communities. Around 180 stalls are being set up to facilitate the display and sale of handicrafts and other products from different States and districts of Karnataka. Interested artisans and producers can apply for stalls, Mr. Khader said.

Focus on AI and technology

The event will also include seminars, discussions, and interactive sessions on the growing use of technology across different sectors.

Producers and other participants will be provided information on artificial intelligence and the adoption of technology to improve their work and businesses, the Minister said.

Open to public

The exhibition will be open to the public from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. during the five-day event. Cultural and entertainment programmes will also be organised.

Mr. Khader appealed to the public to participate in large numbers and make the event a success.

For further information and stall registration, interested persons can contact officials of the Minority Welfare Department or call the helpline on 8277799990, the Minister said.

World.title: Bangladesh to 'positively' consider joining Makkah pact if invited: foreign minister
World.content:
Bangladesh would consider joining the Makkah Pact “positively” if invited by founding members, Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman told parliament on Thursday.

“Joining the pact or not has not come yet, as it is subjected to the intention of the parties involved in the pact. If they invite Bangladesh to join, then we will definitely consider it positively,” the foreign minister said, assuring parliament that Dhaka would assess the potential benefits before making any decision to join.

“More importantly, we have to keep in mind that it [the Makkah Pact] is the Muslim world’s self-defence mechanism,” he added. “And this is our family’s, the Muslim family’s, internal matter. So, there is nothing for others to be concerned about.”

Separately, opposition leader and Bangladesh Jamaat-i-Islami Ameer (chief) Shafiqur Rahman said on Thursday that joining the Makkah Pact was Bangladesh’s “own decision.”

“If Bangladesh takes a decision in the interests and needs of the country and nation, no one else needs to worry about it,” he said in a statement on Facebook.

Earlier this week, Bangladesh’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir said Dhaka had expressed interest in joining the pact.

“If there is one [agreement] in West Asia, if there is a security agreement between Islamic countries, then it is not unusual to go there. Let’s see. The matter is being viewed positively,” said Kabir.

​​​​​​​Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the joint defence agreement at a trilateral summit in Makkah on August 7, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif during the summit at Al-Safa Palace.

The tripartite pact empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them, and reflects their “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

World.title: Claims that CDF Munir visited Iran as envoy for US 'incorrect, misleading': FO
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) on Thursday termed claims that Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir visited Iran as an “envoy” of the United States “misleading and factually incorrect”.

The army chief met the Iranian leadership during his day-long visit to Tehran on August 24, undertaken as part of Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to end the stalemate in the ongoing US-Iran conflict. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had also accompanied him.

Addressing a weekly press briefing in Islamabad on Thursday, FO Spokesperson Tahir Andrabi noted that the discussions held during CDF Munir’s visit to Tehran “focused on regional de-escalation, breaking the military stalemate and exploring a negotiated settlement to restore peace and stability”.

“I will also highlight that claims by certain quarters that the COAS and CDF visited Iran as envoy of President Trump or the US are misleading and factually incorrect, as his visit was undertaken purely in the context and backdrop of Pakistan’s role as a mediator,” he said.

Andrabi asserted that the visit underscored Islamabad’s “sincere and constructive role in bridging the difference between Washington and Tehran”. He noted that the Iranian leadership appreciated Pakistan’s efforts towards de-escalation and peaceful resolution of the conflict.

He stressed that Pakistan “remains engaged alongside our brotherly countries in sincere and concerted efforts towards resolving the crises in the Middle East and Gulf and with respect to the standoff between the US and Iran”.

“Pakistan will continue to actively pursue diplomatic engagement and support all sincere efforts aimed at reviving the peace talks and achieving a comprehensive, just and lasting resolution of the conflict,” he said.

Asked for a comment on the recent US plans for expansion of sanctions on countries doing business with Iran, Andrabi said Pakistan was “following international law and our bilateral trade agreements with Iran”.

“As such, our trade remains in consonance with our obligations,” he affirmed.

Asked about the US’s “economic war” against Iran, Andrabi expressed Islamabad’s hope that “all economic issues will also be settled in the long run” as part of a wider settlement of the US-Iran standoff.

Besides the CDF’s visit, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also remained engaged with his counterparts on regional developments, Andrabi pointed out. He added that over the past two weeks, Dar spoke with Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan three times.

A Pakistan-mediated memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed between the US and Iran in mid-June provided for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and left it up to Tehran and Muscat “to define the future administration and maritime services” in the waterway, in discussion with Gulf states and in line with international law.

But the deal, which was supposed to pave the way for talks on permanently ending the war, has since fallen apart.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi visited Tehran on Tuesday, where he discussed a framework agreement that would establish a “temporary corridor” for shipping and a project to clear mines in the strait.

Although there has been no clear breakthrough yet, and fundamental differences persist between Iran and the US, the latest diplomatic activity has brought the political and technical dimensions of the dispute back into focus.

The Iranian position, nevertheless, remains conditional as it continues to regard the Islamabad MoU as the appropriate framework, but wants Washington to demonstrate through concrete action that it is prepared to honour its commitments.

‘Tangible actions’ needed from Kabul rather than mere assurances: FO

Responding to a query on Afghan Interior Minister Sirajuddin Haqqani’s reported remarks on a proposed security mechanism, Andrabi said: “Pakistan notes the proposal by the interim Afghan government’s interior minister for a dedicated mechanism to address contentious issues.

“We remain open to state-level dialogue. However, the sustainability of any mechanism will depend on tangible actions rather than mere assurances.”

The FO spokesperson emphasised that for any dialogue to take place, the Afghan Taliban must ensure that Afghan soil is not used to perpetrate terrorism against Pakistan.

“Kabul must honour its international commitments, including those under the Doha framework and ensure that Afghan soil is not used by hostile proxies, particularly the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan and the Baloch Liberation Army, against Pakistan,” he said.

Andrabi reiterated that Islamabad remained ready for “institutional coordination provided it results in tangible and verifiable counterterrorism measures and effective border management”.

Asked about rumours that Pakistan had informed China’s special envoy to Afghanistan that it did not desire to hold further negotiations, the FO official said he was not aware of “any such words exchanged between our side and the Chinese envoy”.

He also “categorically denied” the Afghan Taliban’s claim that linked Pakistan to recent developments in Afghanistan’s Badakhshan. He further denied that Pakistan was forming any committee regarding Afghanistan.

On Pakistan’s UN envoy calling Afghan Taliban proxies, Andrabi said: “When their activities are at the behest of a certain neighbouring country to promote terrorism in Pakistan, to promote terrorism by Fitnah Al Hind and Fitnah Al Khwarij, then, unfortunately, we will have to call them proxies, as in doing so, they are not acting in their own interest.”

He observed that “destabilising Pakistan or killing Pakistanis ought not to be the interest of the Afghan regime”.

In the past few years , Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

FO rejects former Indian defence chief’s claims regarding 2025 conflict

Replying to another question, the FO spokesperson rubbished claims made by India’s ex-defence chief, Anil Chauhan, that an Indian Harop drone accidentally struck Kirana Hills near Sargodha during the May 2025 conflict after running critically low on fuel.

“We categorically reject the self-contradictory and retrospective claims made by the former Indian chief of defence staff regarding Kirana Hills,” Andrabi maintained.

He asserted that during the conflict, “Pakistan’s layered air defence network effectively thwarted India’s military objectives, while Pakistan’s subsequent response under Operation Bunyanum Marsoos demonstrated our ability to impose cost across the conflict spectrum”.

“No strategic asset or sensitive infrastructure was compromised in Pakistan. Attempts to retrospectively recast these events through selective narrative or dramatised production cannot alter the verifiable operational record of May 2025,” he said.

The FO spokesperson said that history is “established by facts and evidence, not by Bollywood-style retrospective claims”.

“These post-facto punches, if I may call them, 16 or 17 months after the war would be better directed at their faces,” he added.

Regarding a question about the removal of the structures outside Pakistan’s High Commission in New Delhi, Andrabi said Islamabad has “launched a strong protest” and termed the act a violation of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations.

The FO spokesperson noted that Indian “authorities used heavy machinery to demolish sheds, benches, and a walkway adjacent to the consular section” of the High Commission. He added that the facility was used by those seeking consular assistance and visas.

He pointed out that Indian actions against Pakistan’s High Commission in New Delhi were initiated “without prior notice, and therefore cannot be equated with the actions here in Islamabad”.

“Any attempt to link this incident to Islamabad’s ongoing non-discriminatory anti-encroachment drive in the Diplomatic Enclave is misleading,” Andrabi stated, noting that a notification was given to the Indian side but it “failed to remove such structures”.

He stressed that the drive “targets unauthorised structures outside all diplomatic missions, not just India, in the Diplomatic Enclave”.

Asked about a US panel’s concerns over the visit of the chief of Hindu nationalist group Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), Andrabi refrained from commenting on his US trip.

However, he noted that RSS and “its affiliates and cadres have been fomenting anti-Muslim hatred in India”.

“We hope that organisations and individuals with a conscience in the US will take up these issues with the leader of the RSS if he is visiting the US. I have no particular comment to make on his US visit per se.”

Makkah pact an ‘evolving security architecture’

Asked about Bangladesh’s interest in joining the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA) between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, the FO spokesperson said: “As an evolving security architecture, the MJDA remains open to countries who share their commitments to collective obligations and common security interests.”

The joint defence agreement signed on August 7 aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Andrabi stressed that the pact is a “defensive framework aimed at safeguarding peace and promoting regional stability”.

He added that any formal request by another country to join the pact will be considered in consultation with Riyadh and Ankara.

“The operationalisation of the MJDA, however, remains at an early stage,” he said.

World.title: CDF Munir, Kuwaiti delegation vow to strengthen 'mutually beneficial defence partnership'
World.content:
Pakistan and Kuwait reaffirmed the resolve to “consolidate their historic and brotherly relations into a strong, enduring and mutually beneficial defence partnership”, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Thursday.

A Kuwaiti delegation led by Defence Minister Sheikh Abdullah Ali Abdullah Al-Saleem Al-Sabah met Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi, ISPR said in a statement.

The Kuwaiti minister was accompanied by Chief of General Staff of the Armed Forces Lt Gen Khaled Darj Saad Al-Shriaan.

The two sides discussed “matters of mutual interest, regional security and bilateral defence cooperation”, ISPR said.

“Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing institutional ties and expanding mutually beneficial defence collaboration between the two brotherly countries.”

ISPR added that “the Kuwaiti delegation appreciated the professionalism, operational excellence and valuable contributions of the Pakistan Armed Forces towards regional peace and stability”.

The two sides discussed contributing to regional security and stability as well.

Pakistan and Kuwait also signed ‘Protocol Agreement 2026’, “significantly expanding bilateral military cooperation” under their 2023 Defence Cooperation Agreement, state-run Pakistan TV reported.

The pact was signed during a meeting between the Kuwait defence minister and his Pakistani counterpart Khawaja Asif in Rawalpindi.

“Pakistan’s Armed Forces will assist Kuwait in training, capacity building, border management and other mutually agreed areas of defence cooperation,” Pakistan TV added.

The signing comes about a month after Kuwait ratified the 2023 agreement with Pakistan.

Days after the ratification, Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah paid an official visit to Pakistan, where he met CDF Munir and discussed matters of mutual interest and regional security.

Sheikh Jarrah had expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s steadfast support and constructive contribution toward regional peace and stability.

During his visit, which was the first by a Kuwaiti foreign minister in more than five years, Sheikh Jarrah also called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and his Pakistani counterpart Ishaq Dar.

There’s been a noticeable uptick in high-level contacts between the two countries over the past few mon­ths, including exchanges between senior military officials and discussions on expanding defence cooperation, as Kuwait broadened its security partnerships amid continuing volatility across the Gulf.

World.title: DPM Dar, British foreign secretary discuss Indus Waters Treaty, regional security: FO
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar on Thursday met British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, with the two discussing developments related to the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) and the regional security situation, the Foreign Office (FO) said.

The IWT has come under strain since India announced in 2025 that it was placing its treaty obligations in abeyance. The announcement followed an attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir’s Pahalgam that killed 26 tourists — an incident New Delhi blamed on Islamabad without evidence. For its part, Pakistan strongly denied the allegations and called for a neutral investigation.

In a post on X, the FO said DPM Dar, who is in the United Kingdom on a four-day official visit until Aug 28, highlighted India’s “persistent violations of its international obligations” and stressed the importance of upholding international law and treaty commitments during his meeting with the foreign secretary.

The two met in London, where they held delegation-level talks, the FO said.

It added that the two sides reviewed the “full spectrum” of Pakistan-UK bilateral relations.

The two leaders also reached an agreement to establish a “structured mechanism for formal talks between the two foreign ministries to cover all areas of cooperation to further strengthen bilateral ties and regularly review progress in key areas”.

“They underscored the importance of sustained high-level engagement and closer coordination on matters of mutual interest,” the statement added.

It said the two ministers also discussed the situation in the Middle East, with DPM Dar highlighting Pakistan’s diplomatic and mediation efforts in the region and the progress achieved.

Miliband, for his part, lauded Pakistan for its “constructive role and facilitation efforts in promoting dialogue, diplomacy and stability in the Middle East”.

During the meeting, DPM Dar also raised alarm over the “terrorist threats emanating from Afghan soil”, in reference to threats posed by groups operating out of Afghanistan.

“Both sides underscored the importance of sustained engagement in advancing peace, stability and cooperation in the region and beyond,” the FO said.

It added that the two ministers also underscored the importance of the Pakistani diaspora in the UK, with a focus on “further strengthening the longstanding ties and people-to-people links between Pakistan and the UK”.

DPM Dar has held a series of engagements over the past three days, including meeting the head of the International Maritime Organisation, where he had called for “urgent and effective institutional intervention” for the return of 10 Pakistani sailors held captive by Somali pirates.

DPM Dar also interacted with British parliamentarians of Pakistani origin and met the Commonwealth Secretary-General Shirley Botchwey a day earlier.

World.title: Newborn left unclaimed at Pims for two months dies in blaze
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: One of the 14 babies who died in Wednesday’s fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), Islamabad, was a two-month-old boy who had remained unclaimed at the hospital since birth.

The infant had been living at Pims alongside other sick children. His body remains in the hospital mortuary following his death.

He was born on June 21 to a young girl who appeared to be around 15 years old, said a female doctor at Pims who requested anonymity.

The girl reportedly did not have documents to prove her marriage. The doctor told Dawn that hospital staff had asked “her husband and grandmother” to provide proof of marriage, but when they failed to produce the documents, “they left the baby and never returned”.

The doctor said police had been involved in the case since the child’s birth and had refused to hand over the baby to the family until they provided proof of marriage.

“The case was reported for medico-legal follow-up,” the doctor said.
